The Agent Gateway Team
The Agent Gateway team owns the identity-aware infrastructure that connects enterprise AI agents to the tools, data, and services their organizations authorize. Every call from Claude, Agentforce, Codex, and internal/homegrown agents to a resource flows through us. We enforce authorization, isolate credentials, mint the right token per target, and produce the audit trails that security teams rely on.
We are early in a rapidly evolving space. The standards for agent identity (MCP, OAuth token exchange, DCR) are being built under our feet. Our roadmap includes hardening the data plane for on-premises customer deployments, extending policy semantics beyond tool-level allowlists, adding native support for Agent-to-Agent brokered delegation, and scaling to tenants with thousands of virtual MCP servers.
The Senior Software Engineer Opportunity
Okta is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build the Agent Gateway. You will own features and components across the data and control planes, turning technical designs and product requirements into reliable production systems. Working alongside staff engineers, you will implement token exchange, request routing, credential resolution, and policy evaluation as agent identity specifications evolve.
This is a hands-on software development role at the intersection of product, security, and infrastructure. You will ship services that handle agentic traffic reliably and performantly at scale.
What You'll Be Doing
- Build and Ship: Own the implementation of gateway features end-to-end — from virtual MCP server aggregation to token exchange and policy evaluation — with tests, observability, and operational readiness built in.
- Work in the Runtime Path: Write code that handles credentials, tokens, tenant isolation, and audit logging with care. The gateway sits in the critical path for customer agent traffic, so correctness and reliability matter on every change.
- Implement the Protocols: Read and implement MCP, OAuth token exchange, and agent identity specifications, and feed production lessons back into designs and reference implementations.
- Ship With Agentic Tooling: Use Claude, Claude Code, and MCP-connected agents as everyday parts of your workflow across design, code generation, code review, and operations.
- Contribute to Quality: Participate in code review, testing, incident response, and our design-doc culture, and help raise the team's engineering bar.
What You'll Bring to the Role
- Experience: 4+ years building production backend systems, ideally distributed and highly available.
- Technical Depth: Proficiency shipping production services in Java and/or Go.
- Domain Knowledge: Working knowledge of OAuth 2.0 and OIDC, and comfort reading and implementing spec-driven code. Familiarity with RFC 8693 token exchange is a plus.
- Operational Sense: Hands-on experience with service rollouts, feature flags, observability, and incident response.
- Agentic Fluency: Working familiarity with agentic development tools (e.g., Claude Code, MCP servers, AI-assisted code review), with a point of view on where they accelerate work.
- Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to collaborate across a data plane service and a larger identity control plane.
Extra Credit
- Experience building or integrating with an MCP server, an agent framework, or an LLM-facing gateway.
- Prior work on multi-tenant SaaS platforms.
- Exposure to identity, authorization, or edge-of-network services.
- Active participation in standards work in the agent identity space (MCP, OAuth, GNAP, DCR).
- Full-stack or frontend experience for the gateway's admin and configuration surfaces.

Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
Senior Software Engineer
Get to know Okta
Okta is The World’s Identity Company. We free everyone to safely use any technology, anywhere, on any device or app. Our flexible and neutral products, Okta Platform and Auth0 Platform, provide secure access, authentication, and automation, placing identity at the core of business security and growth.
At Okta, we celebrate a variety of perspectives and experiences. We are not looking for someone who checks every single box - we’re looking for lifelong learners and people who can make us better with their unique experiences.
Join our team! We’re building a world where Identity belongs to you..
Auth0
Auth0 is an easy to implement authentication and authorization platform designed by developers for developers. We make access to applications safe, secure, and seamless for the more than 100 million daily logins around the world. Our modern approach to identity enables this Tier 0 global service to deliver convenience, privacy, and security so customers can focus on innovation.
We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build and improve the tools and experiences that enable developers to integrate Auth0 successfully. You will work primarily with JavaScript and TypeScript across browser and Node.js environments.
Job Description:
You understand developers and care deeply about their experience. You know how to design intuitive APIs, libraries, CLIs, SDKs, documentation, and examples that help developers integrate a product quickly, correctly, and securely.
In this role, you will build and maintain developer-facing software for Auth0, including SDKs, libraries, CLI tooling, Quickstarts, code samples, and implementation guidance. You will work closely with engineering, product, documentation, support, developer relations, and community teams to identify and remove friction from the developer journey.
This is primarily a software engineering role, with meaningful opportunities to engage directly with developers, understand their feedback, and represent their needs across Auth0.
You will be:
- Develop and maintain libraries that enable users to integrate seamlessly with Auth0.
- Directly shape and develop our open-source CLIs and SDKs.
- Write, curate, and edit developer resources, including tutorials, examples, guides, and documentation.
- Own Auth0 code samples and implementation guidance, making them clear, structured, discoverable, and useful for both developers and AI agents.
- Improve our Quickstart guides and onboarding experiences.
- Troubleshoot and fix issues with our libraries, SDKs, CLI, and integrations.
- Gather and channel user feedback within the company to improve the Auth0 developer experience.
- Serve as an internal and external subject-matter expert, providing domain knowledge and technical reviews.
- Engage directly with the developer community and share technical expertise at conferences and other technology events.
You'd be a great fit if you:
- Have 5+ years of professional experience with JavaScript and TypeScript, including Node.js development, backend systems, and API specifications.
- Have built and maintained libraries, production-grade CLIs, SDKs, or other tools consumed by developers, with hands-on open-source experience.
- Have strong knowledge of the JavaScript ecosystem, including frontend and backend development and JavaScript testing frameworks.
- Have working knowledge of JavaScript frameworks such as React, Vue, Angular, or Next.js.
- Have shipped and maintained production applications.
- Have a strong understanding of writing, testing, maintaining, debugging, and supporting software.
- Can structure APIs, code, documentation, and examples to be clear and discoverable for both developers and AI agents.
- Are comfortable using AI coding assistants to accelerate development and debugging, while applying human review to verify the accuracy, security, privacy, and maintainability of AI-generated code.
- Understand CI/CD practices and platforms such as GitHub Actions or CircleCI.
- Have demonstrated experience authoring developer documentation, including tutorials, blog posts, guides, or API documentation.
- Communicate effectively in writing and verbally, including when presenting, documenting, and troubleshooting.
- Are self-directed, work effectively independently, and collaborate well in a global team environment.
Bonus points if you have:
- Experience working in distributed teams and work environments.
- Contributed to or maintained open-source projects.
- A technical blog or published articles on JavaScript or related technologies.
- Knowledge of the identity and access management space.
- Experience evaluating AI-generated code or agent behavior for correctness, security, privacy, maintainability, and hallucination risks.
- Experience building tools, SDK plugins, or other capabilities that enhance AI-assisted or agent-driven developer workflows.
- Familiarity with responsible AI practices, data privacy, and secure coding standards.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Performance ( Toronto)
jobs.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
Okta is The World's Identity Company. We free everyone to safely use any technology - anywhere, on any device or app. Our Identity as a Service solution enables secure yet flexible access, authentication, and automation that transforms how people move through the digital world, putting Identity at the heart of business security and growth.
At Okta, we celebrate a variety of perspectives and experiences. We are not looking for someone who checks every single box - we're looking for lifelong learners and people who can make us better with their unique experiences.
The Engineering Opportunity
Okta's Workforce Identity Cloud secures billions of global logins every day. The Platform Scalability team within the Resilience organization owns the speed, efficiency, and scale of Okta's core authentication and authorization service. We analyze and optimize system behavior across every layer of the stack - from virtualized hardware and the JVM, through MySQL query execution, caching, and the edge, up to cloud components (AWS/GCP) and application code - and we build the frameworks that keep the platform fast and protected for thousands of organizations and millions of daily active users.
We are seeking a Senior Back-End Software Engineer to help own the scalability, efficiency, and service protection of our expanding Identity as a Service platform.
You will build traffic-shaping and service-protection frameworks (rate limiting, concurrency limits, query timeouts, read isolation), create tooling and automation that makes latency and resource bottlenecks easy to find, and dig into production metrics to understand how the system behaves under real customer traffic. While SRE and Database Reliability Engineering keep the service up and running, the Platform Scalability team keeps it fast and efficient - and we partner closely with them to get there.
Because we own monitoring of system latency, throughput, and resource utilization, this is not a heads-down coding role: keeping an eye on system health is part of the regular rhythm of the job, alongside project work and deep-dive investigations.
We value iterative development, automated testing, and individual ownership. Join our creative, fast-paced team to work on impactful projects at serious scale.
Job Duties and Responsibilities
- Design and implement backend frameworks that protect and optimize critical system resources, including rate limiting, traffic shaping, concurrency controls, and query timeout enforcement.
- Monitor production latency, throughput, and resource utilization across the database, application, cache, and edge layers; create and maintain meaningful metrics, dashboards, and alerts, often through automated tooling.
- Analyze latency and scalability bottlenecks end-to-end - JVM profiling, thread and heap analysis, SQL query plans, slow logs, and Hibernate behavior - and drive fixes in code, SQL, and configuration.
- Perform capacity and cost-efficiency analysis (for example, determining whether databases and compute are right-sized for current load), participate in weekly metrics reviews, and support onboarding of large customers and high-traffic events.
- Advise engineering teams on scalable, efficient feature design; review pull requests and SQL changes for latency, resource, and scale impact and recommend tuning or refactoring.
- Actively explore and integrate modern AI-driven developer tooling, automated diagnostics, and intelligent monitoring to accelerate latency and capacity investigations, automate analysis of metrics and logs, and reduce toil.
- Write high-quality unit and functional tests and participate in design and code reviews to keep the engineering bar high.
- Participate in on-call rotations handling latency and scale-related customer escalations, rate limit requests, and production incidents; contribute to Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and long-term mitigations.
- Collaborate closely with SRE, Database Reliability Engineering, Architects, QA, Product Owners, and Customer Support to deliver secure and dependable software.
Minimum Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
- 5+ years of experience as a software developer with strong knowledge of Java or a similar language, including a solid understanding of JVM internals, garbage collection, and concurrency.
- Strong experience with relational databases - preferably MySQL and Hibernate - including query optimization, indexing, execution plan analysis, and schema design.
- Proven experience diagnosing and resolving latency, throughput, and scaling bottlenecks in high-availability, multi-tenant SaaS environments.
- Hands-on experience with profiling and observability tools (e.g., Java Flight Recorder, async-profiler, thread/heap dump analysis, Datadog, Splunk, Prometheus/Grafana or similar).
- Working knowledge of cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred, or GCP/Azure) and modern container ecosystems (Docker, Kubernetes).

We are hiring two hands-on architects. One will lead agent execution, harnesses and evaluations. The other will lead backend services, integrations, data and platform reliability. You will write critical code, resolve cross-team decisions and work with engineers through production rollout.
About You
Hands-on builder: You still write production code and test important decisions through implementation.
Practical architect: You choose a small, clear design and make it easy to extend when the product grows.
Trusted partner: You earn confidence through useful code, clear feedback and customer understanding.
What you will be doing
- Define and implement shared contracts for tasks, events, permissions, approvals, evidence and usage.
- Set clear boundaries between model reasoning, agent harnesses, durable workflows and services that enforce authorization.

- Design integrations with OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, including data boundaries, latency, cost, version changes and measured release quality.
- Build reference services for tenant isolation, scoped tool execution, idempotency, long approval waits and verified results.
- Define the transactional and analytics data architecture. Keep PostgreSQL application state separate from the planned ClickHouse or BigQuery analytics layer.
- Connect Product, Applied AI and Platform engineers through clear ownership and practical APIs. Resolve dependencies that slow delivery.
- Write critical implementations, review recovery and security, and guide technical leads through production rollout and customer expansion.
What you will bring to the role
- A record of leading architecture and delivery across multiple engineering teams, with recent production code you personally implemented.
- Deep knowledge of distributed services, API design, data consistency, cloud security and production operations.
- Experience making systems simpler while improving reliability, security or delivery speed.
- The ability to explain design tradeoffs, guide senior engineers and remain accountable through implementation.
- Depth in at least one of the two role areas below, plus the ability to work across the full product.
Role focus
AI systems architect: Build and evaluate agent harnesses, context management, model integrations and quality controls. Relevant experience includes Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Codex SDK, Strands Agents, LangChain Deep Agents, LangGraph or a comparable custom runtime.
Platform architect: Lead backend, connector, security, data and workflow architecture. Bring deep production systems experience and practical knowledge of integrating model-driven workflows.
Our stack
Python FastAPI, React and TypeScript, AWS Amplify, Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda, SQS, EventBridge and API Gateway. Storage uses RDS PostgreSQL, pgvector and S3. Security and operations include KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch and CloudTrail.
We are adding OpenAI and Anthropic model API integrations. An agent harness and a dedicated analytics layer using ClickHouse or BigQuery are planned. You will help choose and implement them.

- Building a new product within a larger enterprise and keeping technical decisions reversible.

You will build the backend and AWS platform that keep these workers running around the clock. The team owns services, connectors, workflow execution, data and production reliability. You will write Python services and infrastructure code that let workers make approved changes and preserve evidence.
About You
Reliable builder: You design for failure and prove that recovery works.
Hands-on engineer: You write production services and improve the tools engineers use every day.
Strong owner: You follow changes through deployment, monitoring and production support.
What you will be doing
- Build Python FastAPI services, data models and reusable connectors for Okta, AWS, ServiceNow and enterprise applications.
- Implement durable execution with Step Functions, SQS and EventBridge. Handle approval waits, rate limits, duplicate events and safe retries.
- Manage PostgreSQL schemas, indexes, query performance and pgvector retrieval. Enforce tenant isolation across APIs, storage and credentials.
- Build model API access for OpenAI, Anthropic and supported AWS paths, including credentials, quotas, timeouts and cost controls.
- Add an analytics pipeline for worker events, traces, tokens, findings and verified outcomes. Evaluate ClickHouse and comparable systems such as BigQuery.
- Create reliable usage records and reconciliation. Prevent retries, duplicate findings and incomplete work from being counted as new outcomes.
- Build deployment pipelines, infrastructure as code, observability and safe release controls across development, staging and production.
- Implement scoped write services, kill switches, audit retention and backup recovery. Test failures and verify that sensitive changes actually took effect.
What you will bring to the role
- Experience building and operating production backend or distributed systems, with strong coding skills in Python or a comparable language.
- Hands-on AWS experience with APIs, queues, containers, networking, IAM and databases.
- Strong SQL and data modeling skills. Experience diagnosing database performance and asynchronous system failures.
- Experience with infrastructure as code, deployment automation, observability and production incident response.
- Sound judgment about customer data, tenant isolation, credentials and safe changes to external systems.
Scope by level
Senior: Own a backend or platform component, including deployment, tests and production operation.
Staff: Lead a domain such as execution, tenant security, data infrastructure or reliability across teams.
Principal: Set shared backend and platform contracts, resolve system tradeoffs and implement foundational services.
Our stack
Python FastAPI, AWS Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Lambda, SQS, EventBridge, API Gateway and containers. Data and security use RDS PostgreSQL, pgvector, S3 Object Lock, KMS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch and CloudTrail. The frontend uses React and AWS Amplify.
OpenAI and Anthropic model integrations are planned. We are also adding an agent harness and dedicated analytics. ClickHouse is a hiring focus for analytics, and BigQuery or equivalent experience is relevant. The harness and analytics choices remain open.
And extra credit for
- ClickHouse, BigQuery or comparable analytics systems, event ingestion and usage metering.
- Multi-tenant SaaS, OAuth, OIDC, SAML, SCIM or enterprise connector development.
- Deploying agent frameworks, including Claude Agent SDK, Codex SDK, Strands Agents, Deep Agents or LangGraph. Prior identity experience is optional.

-
Design and Develop Core Platform Components: Lead the design and development of scalable and reliable microservices and tools that form the backbone of Okta's Continuous Delivery (CD) platform (including components for Spinnaker, Terraform, and custom tooling).
-
Build Infrastructure as Code Automation: Develop sophisticated software solutions and APIs that empower engineering teams to provision and manage infrastructure, execute production changes, and deploy code with high reliability and efficiency.
-
Architect and Implement Deployment Workflows: Contribute to the architectural design and hands-on implementation of robust CD pipelines and Terraform-based IaC workflows, ensuring scalability, reliability, and security for application deployments.
-
Develop High-Quality Automation Software: Write clean, efficient, and well-tested code (primarily in Java, Python, or Go) for microservices with a strong focus on automation, operational excellence, and self-service capabilities.
-
Collaborate for Operational Efficiency: Partner closely with DevOps, SREs, and Product teams to proactively identify operational bottlenecks and manual processes. Then lead software development efforts to deliver scalable, reliable automation solutions.
-
Champion Software Engineering Best Practices: Advocate for and implement industry best practices in software design, development, testing, and deployment to ensure the highest quality and maintainability of our tooling.
-
Integrate Security by Design: Apply and promote security best practices throughout the software development lifecycle for our tooling and infrastructure automation to ensure a secure, compliant operational environment.
-
Enable Self-Service Capabilities: Proactively identify opportunities to build self-service automation for infrastructure provisioning, application deployments, and other operational tasks, reducing manual effort and improving developer velocity and onboarding.
-
Provide Technical Guidance and Mentorship: Serve as a technical mentor and role model for other engineers on the team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and technical excellence in software engineering.

-
7+ years of professional experience in Software Development, with a strong focus on backend systems and distributed applications.
-
5+ years of hands-on experience in Java, Go, Python, or similar backend languages, specifically building scalable and reliable applications.
-
Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining automation tools, platforms, or microservices for cloud environments (AWS, GCP, or similar).
-
Strong understanding of Infrastructure as Code (IaC) principles and practical experience with tools such as Terraform.

Experience with Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) platform development, including familiarity with tools like Spinnaker or similar.
-
Solid understanding of containerization and orchestration technologies such as Kubernetes and ECS, from a software development perspective.
-
Proficient in using Docker and experienced with building applications that interact with underlying Linux and networking fundamentals.
-
Experience with database technologies (MySQL, MongoDB, etc.) in the context of application development and operational management.
-
A strong passion for solving complex operational challenges through innovative software solutions and automation.
-
Excellent communication, collaboration, and leadership skills within a software development context.
-
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
Good to Have:
-
Demonstrated ability to build AI-powered assistants or "copilots" that simplify complex IaC templates (Terraform/Pulumi) for application teams, reducing the cognitive load on developers.

Familiarity with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) architectures to build intelligent platform documentation bots that can diagnose deployment failures or suggest infrastructure optimisations in real-time.

Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. Security Engineer, Customer Identity, Advanced Threat Protection
Get to know Okta
Okta is The World’s Identity Company. We free everyone to safely use any technology—anywhere, on any device or app. Our Workforce and Customer Identity Clouds enable secure yet flexible access, authentication, and automation that transforms how people move through the digital world, putting Identity at the heart of business security and growth.
At Okta, we celebrate a variety of perspectives and experiences. We are not looking for someone who checks every single box - we’re looking for lifelong learners and people who can make us better with their unique experiences.
Join our team! We’re building a world where Identity belongs to you.
The Role
We seek a knowledgeable and research-focused Security Engineer to join a new Advanced Threat Protection team within Auth0 Customer Identity. This role does two things at once: it researches how attackers will use AI against identity systems, and it researches and builds how we use AI to defend our products, our infrastructure, and — most importantly — our customers' tenants.
This role is a key member of the Security team embedded within the Customer Identity product unit and works across multiple functions to get ahead of emerging AI threats, supporting the growth of our global Customer Identity business.
We are an engineering-focused team that seeks to stay on the cutting edge of security technology and the threat landscape. In this role you won't just assess our current AI security offering — you'll research what we should be protecting customers from one to two years ahead, turn that research into concrete protections, and help put AI-assisted defenses into the hands of the teams and customers who protect their tenants.
In this role you will work as part of a globally distributed team of talented engineers who share a passion for security and enjoy solving complex problems at scale. This role works closely with and alongside the members of the broader Okta Security team in support of Okta's company-wide security strategy and Okta’s Secure Identity Commitment.
This is a level-agnostic description; scope, autonomy, and leadership expectations scale with level (Senior through Staff).
Responsibilities:
- Research and lead how we can use AI to protect customer tenants — both proactively (hardening posture before an attack) and during active incidents (accelerating detection, triage, and response)
- Research and build protections against novel AI attacks that Auth0 and Auth0's customers can be subjected to — adversarial ML, prompt injection, abuse of agentic protocols (MCP, A2A, UCP, and emerging equivalents), model and data poisoning — as they apply to identity systems and customer tenants
- Partner with the identity security teams to help customers strengthen their own tenant security posture through AI-assisted defenses
- Research the emerging AI threat landscape and translate it into a forward-looking (12–24 month) view of what we need to protect ourselves and our customers from — then architect, recommend, and build the tooling to get there
- Review and harden Auth0's AI security offering, identifying gaps and recommending mitigations before they're exploited
- Partner across a globally distributed product-aligned team of security engineers to turn research into shipped protections for customer tenants
- Establish and execute a long-term engineering and threat research roadmap for Advanced Threat Protection aligned with company-wide business and security goals.
- Own high-impact security architecture designs and decisions across Auth0 and Okta Customer Identity infrastructure to support long-term threat resilience.
- Drive cross-functional security strategies and partner across engineering, product, and enterprise security leadership across Okta to influence platform-wide standards and policies.
- Actively coach, mentor, and level up Senior (P3) engineers and team members, fostering technical excellence, research discipline, and leadership growth.
What this position is not:
- Dedicated application security, code review, or compliance-focused work
- Reactive patch and vulnerability management as a primary function — this role is about getting ahead of threats, not chasing them
Requirements:
- You have hands-on experience with AI/ML security — attacking, defending, or both (e.g., adversarial ML, LLM/prompt-injection attacks, agentic-system or model abuse), and an interest in using AI to build defenses, not just to study attacks
- 8+ years of experience in security engineering, with a proven track record of setting technical vision, driving cross-organizational initiatives, and leading architectural choices in cloud/product security.
- Demonstrated experience mentoring senior-level engineers, defining multi-quarter technical strategy, driving architectural consensus, and influencing cross-organizational security initiatives.
- You have hands-on development experience — Go preferred — sufficient to prototype tooling, build AI-powered defenses, and operationalize your research
- You have working knowledge and hands-on experience with one or more of the following:
- AWS and/or Azure security
- Kubernetes
- You have strong knowledge of OWASP (including the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications) and secure coding best practices
- You have a strong foundation in secure software development lifecycle best practices
- You have strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to turn research into clear guidance for engineering and product teams
- You have experience working with a globally distributed and remote team
Bonus points if:
- You have published threat research, CVEs, or conference talks in AI/ML security or identity security
- You have built AI/ML-powered security tooling or defensive automation in a production environment
- You have working knowledge and experience with one or more of the following:
- Adversarial ML, model red-teaming, or AI safety research
- The AI agent / MCP ecosystem and its security implications
- Identity and access management
- Full-stack engineering

Authentication tells you who someone is. Authorization decides what they can do, and doing that well at scale is hard. FGA DevEx owns how developers experience both: our SDKs, CLI, IDE plugins, Helm charts and docs, all developed in the open. The FGA group owns its product end to end, from infrastructure to docs, so we move quickly and see our work reach developers.

About the OIN Team
The Okta Integration Network (OIN) is the platform that lets Okta customers discover, connect, and manage third-party applications and identity providers — from single sign-on and provisioning to newer, higher-order integration patterns as the ecosystem of connected software (including AI agents) continues to grow. It's core infrastructure: the workflows OIN powers run continuously for a very large share of Okta's customer base.
Our team builds and operates all of OIN — from the foundational data model, APIs, and security posture every integration in the network is built on, to the tools partners and customers use to build, test, and ship integrations, to the systems that power what those integrations can actually do once connected. In practice that spans connector metadata and provisioning primitives, partner-facing tooling, and the infrastructure work that keeps a very large, long-lived system fast, secure, and easy to extend as the network grows.
We're actively expanding OIN's scope beyond its original SSO-and-provisioning core — including new integration patterns as AI agents and machine-to-machine access become part of the identity landscape, and a lower-friction path for partners to bring new integrations into the network. You'd be joining at a point where the platform's scope is visibly widening, working closely with product, architecture, and design to help figure out what "right" looks like as much as building it.
About the Role
As a Staff Software Engineer on the OIN team, you'll be a technical leader for a platform a very large share of Okta's customers depend on every day. You'll independently own complex, ambiguous problems end-to-end — from technical scoping through design, delivery, and production operation — partnering closely with product, architecture, and design to help figure out what "right" looks like as much as building it. You'll also be expected to raise the technical bar for the engineers around you, not just deliver your own code.
We're looking for self-motivated engineers who think from first principles, take pride in high-quality software, and are genuinely kind and collaborative to work with.
What you'll be doing
- Lead discovery and technical scoping for new requirements, turning ambiguous product asks into a concrete architecture, phased delivery plans, and credible estimates, in close partnership with product, architecture, and design.
- Design and evolve the APIs, data models, and security posture that OIN's integrations depend on, with an eye toward backward compatibility and long-term extensibility.
- Drive technical decisions across ambiguous, multi-team dependencies, aligning stakeholders across engineering, product, and other parts of the business when the "right answer" isn't obvious yet.
- Modernize and evolve a large, long-lived production system incrementally without disrupting the customers and integrations that depend on it every day.
- Maintain a high bar for security, testing, and code quality, including vulnerability remediation and threat-aware design, while keeping a real sense of urgency on customer-impacting work.
- Own the production health of the systems you build by writing root-cause analyses when things break, driving follow-through on the fixes, and building the observability that prevents repeat incidents.
- Champion AI-native engineering practices by using AI coding assistants and AI-augmented workflows as a core part of how you design, build, review, and ship software, and helping the team adopt them well.
- Mentor and raise the technical bar for the engineers around you, and represent the team's technical point of view in cross-functional forums.
What you'll bring to the role
- 8+ years of professional software development experience, with a demonstrated history of technical leadership and mentorship.
- Deep proficiency in Java (our primary backend language) or a comparable strongly-typed backend language/framework, with the judgment to know when and how to modernize a large, long-lived codebase without disrupting the customers depending on it.

- Applies AI tools thoughtfully across the development lifecycle, from code generation to review to testing, and can help a team adopt them well, not just use them personally.
- Excellent written communication — you bring structure to ambiguous problems and drive them to closure using first principles, in writing that others can act on without you in the room.
Extra credit

About the Team
Authentication tells you who someone is. Authorization decides what they can do, and doing that well at scale is hard. Role-based access breaks down as applications grow, and AI agents are changing who, and what, asks for access. Auth0 FGA solves this with fine-grained authorization. Its engine is OpenFGA, a CNCF incubating open source project that Okta maintains with contributors from other companies, and Auth0 FGA runs that same engine as a managed service.
FGA DevEx owns how developers experience both: our SDKs, CLI, IDE plugins, Helm charts and docs, all developed in the open. The FGA group owns its product end to end, from infrastructure to docs, so we move quickly and see our work reach developers.
Our guiding principle: one developer experience, many deployment models.
About the role
We're hiring a Staff Engineer to set the technical direction for everything the team owns, and to mentor the senior engineers who build it, starting with our SDKs in Go, JavaScript, .NET, Python, Java and more. From there, you'll shape where the developer experience goes next, from how our SDKs evolve to new surfaces like MCP servers. You'll partner with the Core team on API design, so every new capability feels natural in each language.
This is an individual contributor role. You'll work closely with the engineering manager, who owns people and delivery
Responsibilities
Set the direction:
- Define and drive the technical direction for FGA DevEx across open source and SaaS, and turn it into a roadmap with the engineering manager and the product team.
- Build support for that direction across the team, the FGA group and open source community
- Mentor the team's senior engineers, and raise the level of everyone around you.
- Establish how a new team builds software, from design reviews and coding standards to how we test and ship, and set the quality bar.
- Make the calls that are hard to undo: when an API is ready to ship across every language, how it evolves, and when to deprecate.
- Be the voice of developer experience across FGA: partner with the Core team on API design and with internal teams such as Integrations, and flag developer friction wherever you see it.
Own the Platform:
- Architect our SDKs in Go, JavaScript, .NET, Python and Java, including the generator every client is built from.
- Set the standards every SDK follows, from authentication and error handling to retries and rate limiting.
- Shape the tooling and content around the SDKs: the CLI, IDE integrations, Helm charts, GitHub automation, docs and examples.
- Drive the release and versioning strategy across all divisions
- Grow our open source community: build the contributor and maintainer base beyond the team today, and make it easy for outside developers to contribute.
Requirements
- 8+ years as a software engineer, including time leading the technical direction of a team or a significant area, with or without the title.
- Strong proficiency in at least one of Go, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#/.NET, Python or Java, and the curiosity to work across several.
- Experience building software other developers use: SDKs, API clients, libraries, developer platforms, CLIs or tooling.
- A strong sense of API design and ergonomics, and of how an interface should feel in different languages
- Clear communication and a track record of influencing decisions across teams and with outside contributors, without relying on authority
Nice to have
- Contributing to, maintaining or leading open source projects.
- Building with code generation tools such as OpenAPI Generator and templating frameworks.
- Designing resilient clients: authentication flows, retries and rate limiting.
- Setting up GitHub Actions and release automation.
- Working in authorization or identity, such as OAuth, RBAC or ReBAC.

- Experience with monitoring, logging, and alerting tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch, and ELK Stack.

- Understanding of security best practices for cloud platforms and Kubernetes (e.g., role-based access control (RBAC), encryption, and compliance frameworks).

jobs.title: Staff UX Designer
jobs.description:
Secure Every Identity, from AI to Human
Identity is the key to unlocking the potential of AI. Okta secures AI by building the trusted, neutral infrastructure that enables organizations to safely embrace this new era. This work requires a relentless drive to solve complex challenges with real-world stakes. We are looking for builders and owners who operate with speed and urgency and execute with excellence.
This is an opportunity to do career-defining work. We're all in on this mission. If you are too, let's talk.
The Overview
At Okta, we're building a world where anyone can safely use any technology, and we're specifically focused on protecting the future of work. We bring simple and secure access to people and organizations everywhere, promising to not only protect the identities of our customers' workforce and users but to ask, “what more can we make possible?”
As a Staff Product Designer for Okta, you’ll work with a globally distributed design team to apply your craft and expertise on a range of products and services. Our culture provides the opportunity to explore the technologies we’re researching and investing in. Some of your work will be functional, practical user experience design, where you will help our design team drive cohesive user experience across Okta’s portfolio of products. Other work will be speculative, generative explorations that you carry out in collaboration and partnership across the organization to flesh out, frame, and help prioritize solutions in an ever-evolving and complex, often ambiguous, problem space.
The Finer Print
You will lead user experience strategy and execution for our Okta Research & Development (ORD) business unit. Specifically, ORD will solve every identity use case at work – for all types of people (employees, business partners, contractors, frontline workers), for all types of resources (SaaS, servers, privileged resources, machines, etc.), for the largest and most secure businesses in the world. As a designer, your focus will be on helping us build a secure, trusted, and unified platform with deep integrations.
In this role, you have the opportunity to:
- Lead a holistic, human-centered approach to design.
- Guide and oversee the UX strategy alongside cross-functional partners, collaborating to take products from concept to launch and define the long-term strategy for your product area.
- Design and facilitate co-creation design workshops with Product Management, Engineering, and Design to define opportunities within our products to solve valuable customer problems.
- Craft user-centered artifacts and end-to-end journeys to align teams contributing to Workforce Identity Management around the broader user experience.
- Collaborate with other Okta designers to ensure consistency across interface experiences across different user scenarios.
- Inspire teams to think bigger and act smaller, instilling an iterative process and fail-forward mentality to design simple and delightful user interfaces for new and existing Okta products.
- Advocate, mentor, and educate on the benefits of design thinking to product teams and new designers alike; partnering with UX team members to uphold our principles and standards.
- Mentor junior designers and contribute toward team-level and design practice and process improvements.
- Work with Design Leadership to define and drive the frameworks, contracts, and standards for others to be able to then build on top of and add value to, ensuring the quality of UX delivery.
- Find creative ways to continuously learn from customers and users; collaborating with user researchers to research and synthesize user needs to help conceive, define, test, and evolve solutions for our users across a range of mediums and experiences; Advocate for users and deliver user and customer outcomes in a dynamic work environment.
- Help product designers create success metrics to illustrate a clear understanding of how their designs impact customers.
- Present work, concepts, and new ideas to cross-functional team members, adjacent teams, and senior leadership; working to distill complex technical problems into clear, conceptual models and simple, elegant solutions.
- Keep abreast of competitor products and industry trends, including the practical application of AI in the design process; Perform competitive and comparative analysis to understand existing patterns.
Who We Are Looking For
- You have experience leading cross-discipline teams and exemplify leadership.
- You are passionate about solving complex problems, crafting and sharing product and design UX principles to help teams deliver cohesive user experiences.
- You are great at collaborating, sharing work early and often, and seeking constructive feedback from peers and stakeholders.
- You are a pragmatist who actively uses AI tools to improve and accelerate your day-to-day design workflow.
- Demonstrated, hands-on experience using AI-powered design tools (e.g., for ideation, asset generation, or prototyping) in your daily design activities.
- You have the heart of a teacher and can help mentor and train people. You build and share empathy with people to deeply understand them and their needs.
- You are a thought leader, undertaking explorations into new technologies and territories while also delivering practical designs.

About the role:
Agents are becoming first-class users of the internet. They sign in, call APIs, deploy code, and act on behalf of people and teams. That raises questions the web was never designed to answer: Who is this agent? Who does it work for? What is it allowed to do, for how long, and how do we know?
As an engineer on the Agent Auth and Identity team, you'll help answer those questions. You'll build the systems that let agents and people authenticate, delegate access, and act safely across Vercel and the services our customers connect to. This is foundational work: identity and authorization sit underneath everything we ship, and getting them right for agents will shape how modern software gets built.
The scope is intentionally broad. You might spend one quarter designing how credentials are issued and scoped for autonomous agents, and the next building the developer-facing APIs and SDKs that make secure auth feel effortless. You'll own systems end-to-end, from design through long-term operation in production.
We're looking for engineers who care deeply about security and developer experience in equal measure, enjoy working on problems without established playbooks, and want to define how trust works in an agentic world. This is a hybrid role based in San Francisco, in the office on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday.
What you'll do:
- Design, build, and operate the identity, authentication, and authorization systems that power Vercel and our Customers for both people and agents.
- Shape how agents prove who they are, act on behalf of users and teams, and receive scoped, time-bound, auditable access.
- Build secure, scalable APIs, services, and SDKs that make auth simple for developers and their agents to adopt.
- Work with modern and emerging standards (such as OAuth 2.x, OIDC, and agent-focused protocols) and help influence where they go next.
- Lead projects end-to-end: identify opportunities, set technical direction, and deliver improvements in security, reliability, and developer experience.

About the role
The CDN Content team is responsible for serving all content that flows through Vercel's global CDN — static assets, optimized images, incrementally regenerated pages, partially prerendered shells, and everything in between — to billions of requests for millions of developers. Our focus is performance: ensuring content is served globally as fast as possible. Caching plays a big role in making that happen, and the team operates a multi-tier caching architecture spanning in-process caches, regional cache services, and object storage across 20+ regions.
As a Software Engineer on the team, you'll take on well-scoped projects with real production impact and grow into owning larger pieces of the system. The work spans the serving path end to end, and everything ships through careful, progressive rollouts validated with production data. You'll learn how a planet-scale CDN works from engineers who built it.
This is a team where infrastructure meets product: we work in close partnership with frameworks such as Next.js, bringing framework-defined infrastructure to life on Vercel's CDN, and the serving and caching behavior we ship directly shapes the performance and cost that millions of developers see. You'll develop strong instincts for distributed systems, careful production rollouts, and data-driven engineering.

If you're located beyond that distance, the role is fully remote. For location-specific details, please connect with our recruiting team.

Vercel Connect helps developers give agents and AI-built apps secure access to the data, tools, and events they need—without wrestling with OAuth, credentials, and integration complexity. We’re currently building two things: 1) a platform for managing agent identity, access and permissions and 2) a set of rich connectors for the 1000s of systems (like Linear, Slack, GitHub, Google, etc.) that agents will need to talk to.
We’re solving core problems like agent identity and delegated access, tool approval and standards around making agents aware of changes on 3rd party platforms.
As a senior engineer on this team you'll not only own our APIs, token infrastructure, authorization, SDKs, and more, but work with external companies to make it easier for developers to build agents that integrate with their products. You’ll need to balance both high uptime and fast performance with flexibility to allow for seamless connection to many systems that weren’t designed with agents in mind. If you’re looking for a role that will put you at the center of how agent identity and credentials work, this is it! This is a hybrid role based in San Francisco, in the office on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday.

- Ship provider integrations end to end — auth flows, token exchange, app registration, and the configuration UI — from generic API-key and OAuth presets through bespoke cases like Snowflake Partner Connect, Slack manager apps, and Microsoft Entra.
- Own and improve our infrastructure (uptime, performance, secure storage of credentials and keys) and developer experience for Connect
- Work with industry leaders within and outside of Vercel to propose and implement new authentication and authorization protocols for AI era
- Build and harden event forwarding — signature verification inbound, project-scoped identity outbound, delivered to the right deployment and environment.
- Make Connect the obvious way to give an agent a credential, extending the SDKs , consent-redirect flow, and framework adapters.
- Reduce the cost of the next hundred integrations, so most new providers become configuration rather than code.

jobs.title: Senior Staff Data Scientist
jobs.description:
About the Team:
Netlify’s Data team helps the company understand and improve the full product-led growth journey, from activation and engagement through conversion, retention, and monetization. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Growth to uncover opportunities, evaluate investments, and understand what drives customer and business outcomes.
We’re hiring a Senior Staff Data Scientist to deepen how data shapes our product and growth strategy. You’ll develop an end-to-end understanding of the PLG journey, proactively identify opportunities, and turn complex data into hypotheses, experiments, and recommendations that influence where we invest and what we build. This is a highly autonomous role for someone who can move from identifying an important question to shaping the approach, defining success, and driving toward an answer.
What You'll Do:
- Own the analytical understanding of Netlify’s PLG performance across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention, identifying opportunities before they become requests
- Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to turn behavioral insights into product bets, defining what to test, how to measure it, and what the results mean
- Lead experimentation from hypothesis through decision, including study design, methodology, success metrics, guardrails, analysis, and recommendations
- Apply statistical rigor where it matters while recognizing when there is enough signal to make a decision and move forward, and help teams develop that same judgment
- Build scalable analytical systems like semantic models, trusted metrics, proactive monitoring, and AI-powered agents that surface opportunities without waiting to be asked
- Use AI to investigate faster, automate recurring analytical work, and test more hypotheses without sacrificing the judgment that makes the output useful
- Identify gaps in measurement, event instrumentation, and metric definitions, and partner with Data and Product Engineering to close them
- Serve as a trusted analytical partner to PLG leadership, using evidence and product judgment to influence investment decisions and roadmap priorities
- Influence product strategy through evidence, product instincts, and a clear point of view, without relying on formal authority to do it
What You'll Bring:
- 8+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, or data science, with a track record of high ownership and measurable impact on PLG or consumer product outcomes
- Deep understanding of product and growth dynamics across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention
- Demonstrated ability to turn behavioral data into product hypotheses and carry them from insight through experimentation and measured outcomes
- Deep experimentation expertise: study design, statistical reasoning, causal inference, and the judgment to know when an experiment has told you what you need to know
- Experience building analytical systems such as metrics layers, monitoring frameworks, or semantic models that teams can rely on over time
- An AI-native approach to analysis: you use AI tools actively to accelerate investigation, automate repetitive work, and surface patterns faster
- A track record of influencing senior stakeholders and product direction through analytical reasoning, clear recommendations, and sound judgment
- Comfort operating with significant autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces, including determining which questions are most important to answer
- Strong written and verbal communication skills in distributed environments, with the ability to make complex findings clear and recommendations actionable
This Role is a Great Fit If:
- You're energized by finding the opportunity before anyone thought to ask - proactive discovery is how you naturally work, not a mode you shift into
- You think like a product person who happens to be exceptionally rigorous with data, not a data person who occasionally weighs in on product
- You thrive when the problem isn't handed to you - you'd rather define the question worth asking than answer the one that landed in your queue
- You get excited about building systems that keep working after you've moved on to the next problem
- You're comfortable making a call with imperfect information and can articulate clearly why you made it
- You enjoy being a thought partner to senior leaders - shaping how they think about investment and opportunity, not just supporting decisions already made
- You work well in a remote-first, async environment where written clarity and self-direction matter more than proximity
- You're drawn to roles where the measure of success is outcomes, decisions made, bets tested, metrics moved, not volume of output produced
Applying
Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway!
When applying please include:
A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts.
Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com.
About Netlify
Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. Now, as we embrace the next era of software development, we are embedding the same fluid, intuitive experience into the Agent Experience (AX), making it just as simple for intelligent agents to understand, interact with, and act on our platform as it is for developers. Whether your user is human or machine, Netlify ensures the path from idea to URL is seamless, fast, and deeply reliable.
We are a Series D company that has raised over $200M from investors such as Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, EQT, Bessemer, BOND, and Menlo Ventures. As a fully distributed company, we aim to create a company culture where the best idea can come from anywhere and strive to be thoughtful, compassionate, and collaborative in our work. If this sounds like something you’d like to be part of, we’re excited to connect with you!
At Netlify, we are committed to a compensation philosophy that prioritizes fairness and equity, positions our employee compensation competitively in the market, recognizes and rewards performance, and takes a comprehensive approach to our rewards package. We anchor our compensation philosophy on a market-based approach, therefore salary ranges may differ depending on the labor cost in a particular location. The salary provided is in addition to robust benefits and participation in Netlify’s equity plan. Our hiring range for this role is targeted at $204,000 - $275,000 for most US-based locations. Candidates outside the US or in premium markets should consult with their Talent Acquisition partner regarding location-based ranges, as they may be higher or lower than the average US range listed. The starting pay will be determined based on multiple factors, including expertise and skills, market demands, experience, internal equity, and applicable geographic location. These compensation packages and ranges are subject to change and may be modified in the future.

jobs.description:

Our APIs meet critical business needs. Customers deploy them during active attacks, automate them through Terraform and CI/CD, and build entire security workflows on top of them. When the threat landscape moves, our APIs are how customers move with it. A bad release here leaves them exposed when they need us most: a great one is invisible, and that's the bar.

jobs.description:
Fastly helps people stay better connected with the things they love. Fastly’s edge cloud platform enables customers to create great digital experiences quickly, securely, and reliably by processing, serving, and securing our customers’ applications as close to their end-users as possible — at the edge of the Internet. The platform is designed to take advantage of the modern internet, to be programmable, and to support agile software development. Fastly’s customers include many of the world’s most prominent companies, including GitHub, Yelp, Paramount, and JetBlue.

Posting Open Date: Sep 21st, 2026
Anticipated Posting Close Date*: Nov 30, 2026
*Job posting may close early due to the volume of applicants.
Senior Technical Product Manager, API Traffic and Enforcement
APIs are how software talks to software, and the volume and variety of that traffic is growing rapidly. AI agents now discover and call APIs directly, and MCP servers are a new kind of endpoint with the same questions attached: what exists, what it's supposed to do, and who is allowed to call it. Enterprises are challenged to respond to those questions. This role owns Fastly's answer.
As a Senior Technical Product Manager on Fastly's Core Infrastructure Product Management team, you will own how Fastly defines what traffic is allowed and how traffic is held to that definition. That means our customers' API surface end to end – discovery and inventory of the APIs they actually run, the schemas that describe intended behavior, and the API gateway itself – and the enforcement primitives underneath it, including ACLs, allowlists, rate limiting, and the request-path controls that turn a declared model into something the platform actually enforces. Much of security is about detecting the bad. Your charter is the other half: defining what good looks like and enforcing it.
Customer APIs are the first and largest surface for the positive model, and the primitives you own are the ones other products adopt as that model extends across the platform. This role reports to the Director of Core Infrastructure Product Management and has real latitude to set direction.
What You'll Do:
- Own the positive model end to end: drive the strategy and roadmap for defining what traffic is allowed. You will take customers from not knowing what APIs they run, to describing intended behavior precisely, to enforcing it in the request path.
- Make API discovery tell customers something they didn't know: own discovery and inventory across the API surfaces customers actually operate. Discovery is where most customers start, and how good it is determines whether they trust anything built on top of it.
- Turn schemas into enforceable contracts: own schema definition, generation, and validation. When customers can't hand you an accurate spec for their own APIs, the product has to produce one worth enforcing against, then keep it accurate as their APIs change.
- Own enforcement in the request path: ACLs, allowlists, rate limiting, and the controls that turn a declared model into something the platform enforces, along with the gateway that applies them. Build these as primitives other products can adopt, not features scoped to one surface.
- Make agents first-class: agents calling APIs are a new kind of client, and MCP servers are a new kind of endpoint. Define how Fastly identifies them, authorizes them, and holds them to allowed behavior.
- Take and defend clear positions: bring evidence-based points of view on how traffic should be described and constrained, and drive them to decisions across engineering, product, and partner teams. You will bring structure to ambiguous problems and move decisions forward earlier.
What We're Looking For:
- Experience: 5+ years in product management or technical product leadership, ideally on API, security, or platform infrastructure products.
- API and request-path fluency: you understand how API traffic is described, validated, and constrained — schemas and specs, gateway behavior, and the difference between allowlist models and detection-based ones. You can reason about where each fits and what it costs to run.
- Platform thinking: a track record of building capabilities that serve more than one product or team. Shared primitives, enforcement points, or controls others build on, rather than features scoped to a single surface.
- Execution focus: a demonstrated bias for shipping. You are hands-on and comfortable owning outcomes in ambiguous, fast-moving conditions rather than waiting for perfect clarity.
- Conviction and influence: the ability to form clear, evidence-based positions and defend them across engineering and product partners, including pushing back constructively. You build alignment without relying on authority.
- Communication and presentation: a clear communicator who can move between deep technical discussion with engineers and crisp framing for customers and executives, with genuine curiosity about the "why" behind a customer's problem. You can stand up in front of a room, make a case, and hold it under questioning.
We’ll be super impressed if you have experience in any of these:
- Hands-on work with API gateways and OpenAPI-driven validation: schema generation from live traffic, drift detection as APIs change, and the gap between the spec a team publishes and what their API actually does.
- The agentic traffic stack — workload and agent identity (SPIFFE/WIMSE, mTLS), OAuth 2.1 for delegated agent authorization, and agent protocols like MCP and its authorization spec.
- Request-path enforcement at scale: WASM filters, eBPF, or policy engines like OPA and Rego.
- Startup or 0-to-1 experience building API, security, or infrastructure products in a fast-moving environment.

- Fastly's internal developer portal, built on Backstage.
- An internal set of tools and data pipelines that synthesize network and financial data to provide insights into network costs, capacity planning, and related business concerns.

- Debug and resolve issues across the software stack, from datacenter hardware to the browser, often spanning multiple services and data sources
- Communicate clearly about the status of your work and any problems you encounter. Write useful updates, ask good questions, and raise issues early rather than at the deadline
- Collaborate with other engineers on the team. Provide thoughtful code review and share context and knowledge.
- Participate constructively in team planning and retrospectives
- Participate in on-call rotation as required, and respond to incidents within the team's SLA while on-call.

Staff Software Engineer, Linux Edge Kernel
Fastly's Kernel and Host Networking team builds and ships the Linux kernel that runs on every server in our global edge network, and every customer request passes through it. As a Staff engineer you own technical problems end to end: from a crash signature or a new NIC on the bench, through root cause and design, to a change that is upstreamed and safely running on thousands of servers. The work spans networking, XDP and eBPF, memory, performance and hardware enablement. It also spans layers. Our kernel is the datapath of a distributed system whose control planes are constantly pushing new state to the fleet, so staying correct under change is part of the job. Formal CS education is not required; demonstrable experience is what matters.
What You'll Do:
- Set technical direction for kernel projects, own them end to end from problem statement to fleet rollout, and mentor engineers on the team
- Take new servers, CPUs and NICs from first boot to full fleet: drivers, IRQ affinity, RSS and queue layout on high core count hosts
- Improve datapath and transport performance with XDP, eBPF and protocol work based on IETF specifications
- Debug problems that cross layers with application teams, such as MTU behavior, cgroup memory accounting and packet filtering
- Develop and maintain kernel changes and Fastly kernel modules on our long term kernel line, and reduce our private delta by upstreaming
- Make sure state pushed from control planes to eBPF and XDP programs is applied, verified and safe to roll back
- Own kernel health in production: triage crashes, WARNs and regressions across the fleet, find the root cause and ship the fix
- Own and improve the kernel release process and the signals behind it: CI, bake, canary, staged rollout and rollback across thousands of servers, plus crash metrics and drift detection that fire before customers notice
- Join the on-call rotation, lead the kernel side of incidents and drive follow-up actions to closure
What We're Looking For:
- 7+ years of related engineering experience, including substantial production C, with 3 of those years leading technical projects
- Production Linux kernel development, including debugging use-after-free, refcount and leak bugs with KASAN, kdump, ftrace, perf or bpftrace
- Working knowledge of the scheduler and memory management (EEVDF, memcg)
- Experience managing a kernel patch stack and working with upstream communities
- Solid understanding of the Linux network stack (TCP/IP, sk_buff lifecycle, qdiscs, NIC drivers) and XDP or eBPF, with deep expertise in at least one of these areas
- Operational discipline: staged rollouts, canaries, kill switches, observability, postmortems and closing action items
- Understanding of distributed systems: control plane and datapath consistency, partial failure and safe config rollout at fleet scale
- Ability to design broadly scoped work and drive it across teams
We’ll be super impressed if you have experience in any of these:
- Upstream kernel contributions or subsystem maintainership
- Deep Knowledge of Transport protocols from IETF RFCs: QUIC, TCP, ECN and L4S, MASQUE
- Hardware enablement on AMD EPYC or Intel platforms, and NIC drivers such as mlx5, ice or i40e
- Load balancing or traffic steering systems
- CDN or large edge network environments
- Container networking: network namespaces, veth, cgroups, and eBPF-based CNI datapaths

This position requires availability during core business hours and participation in an on-call rotation.

jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
jobs.description:
PagerDuty, Inc. (NYSE: PD) is the global leader in AI-first digital operations. By automatically detecting, diagnosing, and remediating issues, the PagerDuty Platform orchestrates AI agents and automated workflows with context from over 750 integrations. Trusted by approximately two-thirds of the Fortune 100 and nearly half of the Fortune 500, PagerDuty is the industry standard for organizations scaling resilient, autonomous operations. Notable customers include Chipotle, Cloudflare, Docusign, Fox, Nvidia, Salesforce, Spotify, Zoom and more. We are growing rapidly and hiring top talent with leading AI skills across engineering, sales, product, marketing, and beyond as we build the leading digital operations platform.
About the role
PagerDuty’s Operations Cloud runs on a platform that ingests billions of signals and turns them into real-time action for thousands of customers. We’re looking for a Senior AI/ML Engineer who lives at the intersection of two disciplines: large-scale distributed systems and applied AI.
In this role you will design and ship AI systems that run in production at PagerDuty’s scale — powering Incident Management AI Agents, event intelligence, and the LLM-powered capabilities embedded across our platform. You’ll own the full lifecycle, from framing the problem to serving reliably at scale.
We are looking for a candidate who is genuinely passionate about building with modern AI — LLMs, agents, and retrieval — but grounded in the realities of building resilient, high-throughput systems.
What you’ll do
- Design and build AI-powered features — LLM agents, retrieval, and event intelligence — that operate on high-volume, real-time event streams, from problem framing through production deployment and monitoring.
- Architect and own the systems behind them: agent and prompt orchestration, retrieval pipelines, tool/API integrations, and low-latency inference and evaluation at scale.
- Reason about consistency, throughput, fault tolerance, and cost across services that must stay reliable under bursty, unpredictable load.
- Take AI features from prototype to production, establishing the evaluation, guardrail, observability, and improvement loops that keep them accurate and trustworthy over time.
- Partner with platform, product, and applied-research teams to define what “good” looks like and to integrate AI cleanly into existing services.
- Raise the bar through example, reviews and mentorship, and help shape the team’s technical direction.
What you’ll bring
- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with meaningful time spent building and operating production distributed systems (high-throughput services, streaming/event-driven architectures, or large-scale data platforms).
- Hands-on experience building and shipping AI systems in production — LLM-powered applications, agents, or retrieval — including the surrounding orchestration, serving, and evaluation, not just prototypes.
- Strong programming fundamentals and comfort moving between systems and AI/application code.
- Solid grounding in applied AI fundamentals: prompting, retrieval, agent patterns, and how to evaluate and guardrail LLM behavior.
- Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP, or Azure), containers, and orchestration (Kubernetes).
- A pragmatic, reliability-minded mindset: you optimize for systems that work correctly at scale, and you can articulate the trade-offs behind your choices.
- Strong communication and collaboration skills, and a track record of raising the quality of the teams and systems around you.
Nice to have
- Experience with LLMOps tooling and patterns — evaluation harnesses, prompt/version management, tracing and observability for agents, and online/offline eval consistency.
- Deep experience serving LLM-based systems in production, including retrieval-augmented generation, multi-step agents, and tool use.
- Background in anomaly detection, event correlation, or applied problems in observability, AIOps, or reliability.
- Familiarity with the ecosystem — e.g. LLM APIs and frameworks such as LangChain or LlamaIndex, vector databases, and distributed data/compute tools such as Kafka, Airflow, or Spark.
- Contributions to open-source AI or distributed-systems projects.
Why PagerDuty
At PagerDuty, AI it’s core to how we help the world’s teams keep their digital services running. You’ll work on problems where scale, latency, and correctness genuinely matter, alongside engineers who care about building systems that people depend on in their most critical moments.
