jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
This is a remote opportunity, and we would be interested in applicants located in the US or Canada.
The Opportunity:
At Grafana Labs, we build observability tools that help users understand, respond to, and improve their systems – regardless of scale, complexity, or tech stack. We recently started a skunkworks initiative with a mission to bring observability to the rest of the business. Our goal is to make Grafana the single best place where humans and AI agents understand and act on real-time data from across the enterprise. As part of this initiative, we are building an AI-native data intelligence system that gives agents reliable, governed access to enterprise context. This system helps agents retrieve the right data, metadata, definitions, lineage, quality signals, and institutional knowledge without every agent builder having to maintain their own brittle context files. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence.
The new team is a mix of seasoned Grafanistas and new hires. We operate with a high degree of autonomy and ownership, both as individuals and as a team. Engineers are empowered to make decisions, move quickly, and validate ideas early – while being supported by a deeply collaborative culture that values curiosity, feedback, and cross-functional partnership.
We’re looking for a Senior Software (Database) Engineer to help build the underlying storage system for our general purpose data platform. The database layer has both OLAP and OTLP capabilities to support classic analytics queries while also serving up freshly stored data. It embraces the separation of compute and storage and is designed to run on multiple cloud providers. This is an early-stage role on a high-autonomy team, so you should be comfortable working through ambiguity, making pragmatic architectural decisions, and building systems that can evolve from internal dogfooding to production-grade SaaS. As the team matures, there’s a broad opportunity to expand or redefine this role based on impact and initiative.
What You'll Be Doing:
- Take ownership over and build one or multiple parts of the database: Design, implement, test, and operate ingestion, query planning, distributed query execution, data formats, storage formats.
- Create a scalable SaaS foundation: Help define and build the architecture for a multi-tenant database service, including tenant isolation, usage tracking, quotas, audit logs, background jobs, and reliable service boundaries.
- Power agent-facing retrieval workflows: Build APIs and database interfaces that allow AI agents, MCP tools, CLIs, and internal applications to retrieve data quickly.
- Work across product and infrastructure: Partner with the team to make practical tradeoffs between fast experimentation and long-term reliability, especially as the project moves from prototype to production.
- Operate what you build: Instrument database services with metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and dashboards. Use observability tools to understand system behavior and improve reliability.
- Contribute to technical direction: Help shape the architecture, service boundaries, storage choices, API contracts, deployment patterns, and engineering practices for a new product area.
- Effective communication: You’ll be working in a highly dynamic and collaborative environment, so we need someone who can communicate effectively and contribute across teams.
- Ownership and impact: Take full ownership of the database solutions you develop, ensuring they are not only innovative but also scalable, maintainable, and aligned with real user workflows.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
- Strong engineering skills: Solid experience building production-grade, user-facing software systems. You’re a self-starter, capable of tackling complex engineering problems and making design decisions with minimal supervision.
- AI experience with a practical mindset: You’re familiar with AI technologies and frameworks, and you focus on delivering high-quality solutions that work in the real world, not just in theory.
- Quick iteration and experimentation: You’re comfortable releasing prototypes, collecting feedback, and iterating with a pragmatic mindset.
- Proven initiative: You take ownership and drive projects forward, pushing boundaries to find the most impactful solutions. You can deal with ambiguity and are able to define scope where things are loosely defined.
- Collaborative attitude: You communicate effectively with your peers. You’re open to feedback, and you bring a solutions-oriented mindset to the table.
- Experience with distributed systems, catalogs and table formats, query engines.
- Mastery of a programming language like golang, C++, or Rust
- Proven track record of delivering software that made it into production and is actively used by users.
- Exposure to working in cloud-native environments (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure).
- Experience using observability tools to understand and troubleshoot system behavior.
Bonus Points for:
- Experience building distributed query engines.
- Experience building data warehouses and/or data lakes.
- Experience building tools for data engineering.
How we work:
We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our Staff engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product.
Compensation & Rewards:
In Canada, the Base compensation range for this role is $164,490 - $197,389. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.
*Compensation ranges are country specific. If you are applying for this role from a different location than listed above, your recruiter will discuss your specific market’s defined pay range & benefits at the beginning of the process.
Why You’ll Thrive at Grafana Labs:
- 100% Remote, Global Culture - As a remote-only company, we bring together talent from around the world, united by a culture of collaboration and shared purpose.
- Scaling Organization – Tackle meaningful work in a high-growth, ever-evolving environment.
- Transparent Communication – Expect open decision-making and regular company-wide updates.
- Innovation-Driven – Autonomy and support to ship great work and try new things.
- Open Source Roots – Built on community-driven values that shape how we work.
- Empowered Teams – High trust, low ego culture that values outcomes over optics.
- Career Growth Pathways – Defined opportunities to grow and develop your career.
- Approachable Leadership – Transparent execs who are involved, visible, and human.
- Passionate People – Join a team of smart, supportive folks who care deeply about what they do.
- In-Person onboarding - We want you to thrive from day 1 with your fellow new ‘Grafanistas’ to learn all about what we do and how we do it.
- Balance is Key - We operate a global annual leave policy of 30 days per annum. 3 days of your annual leave entitlement are reserved for Grafana Shutdown Days to allow the team to really disconnect. *We will comply with local legislation where applicable.
Equal Opportunity Employer: Grafana Labs is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone regardless of race, colour, nationality, origin, caste, sex, gender reassignment identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, religion or belief, disability, veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, maternity, marital, family or carer status, or any other characteristic which is protected by local law. We believe that equality and diversity build a strong organisation, and we work hard to ensure that is the foundation of our organisation as we grow.

We build Tempo, the open-source distributed tracing backend behind Grafana Cloud Traces and Grafana Enterprise Traces (GET). Tempo makes it easy to search traces, generate metrics from spans, and connect tracing data with logs, metrics, and profiles across the Grafana stack.
2026 is an inflection point for Tempo. After a major architectural upgrade and the launch of TraceQL metrics, we are shifting from foundational work to product and operational excellence, and evolving Tempo from a SaaS database into a platform that powers Grafana’s next generation of observability products (App Observability, Asserts, Traces Drilldown, and AI-driven assistants).
Over the next year, you will help us:

Within the Observability department, we build products that help customers understand and troubleshoot their applications and infrastructure. We work closely with product management, design and other engineering squads to provide seamless and highly curated experiences for our customers.
The squad: Database Observability
We build and evolve Grafana Cloud Database Observability. We want to help users understand the health and performance of their databases, identify slow queries and troubleshoot issues through clear, actionable insights.
As a frontend engineer on the squad, you’ll build experiences that make complex database telemetry easy to explore and understand. You’ll work closely with backend engineers, product management and design to take ideas from early exploration through to production and improve them based on customer feedback.
Our frontend stack is primarily TypeScript and React, interacting with backends written in Go. Your primary focus will be frontend engineering, with opportunities to work across the stack, contributing to APIs and backend functionality to deliver complete customer experiences. Frontend engineers at Grafana also have opportunities to contribute to open source communities.

- Own technical projects from problem framing through rollout, including getting user feedback and measuring whether what you shipped actually worked.
- Collaborate with Product Management, Product Design and backend engineers to build intuitive user experiences using clean, reusable components, contributing to supporting APIs and backend functionality where needed.
- Mentor and collaborate with other engineers. Raise the engineering bar through code review, design feedback, pairing on hard problems, and writing that leaves the team better than you found it.
- Participate in on-call for the software you help build, contributing to incident response and learning from incidents.
- Provide technical support in customer escalations and help us identify areas of high friction to address.
- Collaborate with other squads on shared dependencies, contribute to design proposals, and share the team’s work through demos and technical discussions.

- We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind and enjoy working as a team.
- Strong frontend engineering experience, with experience across the stack. You have experience building and maintaining production web applications with React and TypeScript, and are comfortable contributing to backend services and APIs. You value maintainability, readability, automated testing and secure development practices.
- Technical ownership. You have solid experience delivering complex projects, mentoring other engineers and helping teammates work more effectively. You communicate clearly in a fully remote, asynchronous environment.

- User focus and pragmatism. You break complex problems into short feedback loops: analyze, design, deliver an MVP, learn, iterate.

The Opportunity:
As a Senior Full-Stack Engineer on the Grafana Catalog team, you will help grow the Grafana plugin ecosystem. Plugins are how Grafana connects to almost any data source, panel type or app, and the catalog has more than 300 of them from Grafana Labs, commercial partners and the open source community.
We own the full plugin lifecycle. Developers build plugins with our tooling, publish them to the catalog, and users discover, install and update them in Grafana and Grafana Cloud. We are also building the Grafana Marketplace, which lets partners and independent developers sell their plugins to Grafana users. It is in pilot today and you will help us take it from there.
What You’ll Be Doing:
Some of the things we own:
- The Grafana Marketplace: paid plugins, publisher onboarding, and how customers buy and get access to them
- The plugin catalog in grafana.com and inside Grafana, where users search, compare and discover plugins
- Plugin installation and management in Grafana and Grafana Cloud
- Plugin delivery: publishing, signing, validation and the CDN that serves plugins to every Grafana Cloud instance
- Plugin review: every plugin published to the catalog goes through our review process before it reaches users
- Developer tooling and developer portal that helps develop the plugins
A typical “day in the life” could include:
- Building new Marketplace features across the Grafana frontend, our Go services and grafana.com
- Improving how users find and install plugins, for both humans and agents like Grafana Assistant
- Making it easier and faster for developers to build, test and publish plugins
- Automating and improving the review process that every published plugin goes through
- Supporting the operations and reliability of plugin installs and delivery in Grafana Cloud
- Talking to plugin developers and partners and turning their feedback into roadmap items
- Coming up with suggestions for process improvements
- Working closely with the rest of the Grafana Division

- You know how to transform ideas into working code, you are able to design a solution, get feedback and deliver large projects.
- You are a self-driven individual who understands the power of feedback loops in making roadmap decisions and driving our product forward.
- You are a motivated self starter with a bias towards action, and willing to take on any challenge
- You are customer focused. We build everything with our users in mind. You have a passion for creating intuitive products that fit customers’ needs.
- You are an excellent communicator and you enjoy collaboration
- You are comfortable working in a remote-first company

- Solid experience with Golang & Typescript
- Experience with React and building user-facing web applications
- Experience with Kubernetes & microservices

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.
We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
This is a remote opportunity and we're interested in candidates based in the US or Canada. Residents of Quebec are not eligible for this role.
Senior Full-Stack Software Engineer, Grafana Data Source Plugins
The Opportunity:
As a Senior Full-Stack Engineer in the Grafana Data Source Plugins squad, you will take a leading role in developing and enhancing a diverse portfolio of data source plugins that retrieve the data powering Grafana dashboards used by teams worldwide.
Our team focuses on continuously improving data source plugins, ensuring seamless experience for human and agent users alike. A key aspect of this role is guaranteeing the smooth operation and reliability of our plugins in the Grafana Cloud, helping us deliver on our commitment to world-class observability tools.
What You’ll Be Doing:
- Some data source plugins we own:
- Prometheus, Loki, Infinity, MySQL, PostgreSQL, AWS Cloudwatch, and Clickhouse. The full catalog is listed here.
- A typical “day in the life” could include:
- Building or improving Grafana plugins to integrate third party services or databases into Grafana
- Supporting the operations and reliability of our plugins in Grafana Cloud
- Coming up with suggestions for process improvements
- Integrating data sources with agentic workflows such as Grafana Assistant
- Providing technical support in customer escalations
- Working closely with the rest of the Grafana Division
What Makes You a Great Fit:
- You know how to transform ideas into working code, you are able to design a solution, get feedback and deliver large projects.
- You are a self-driven individual who understands the power of feedback loops in making roadmap decisions and driving our product forward.
- You are a motivated self starter with a bias towards action, and willing to take on any challenge
- You are customer focused. We build everything with our users in mind. You have a passion for creating intuitive products that fit customers’ needs.
- You are an excellent communicator and you enjoy collaboration
- You are comfortable working in a remote-first company
Requirements:
- Solid experience with Golang & Typescript
- Experience with Kubernetes & microservices
- Experience writing clean, robust, and performant software that is easily maintained by others
- Experience participating in an on-call rotation and performing operations/SRE tasks
Bonus Points For:
- You have been a user of Grafana and Grafana Data Sources
- You have expertise in one of the underlying databases we support
- You have strong experience working with a Product Manager or external stakeholders

Senior Product Designer, Knowledge Graph
This is a remote position based in Canada (East Coast Canada preferred, open to other time zones for exceptional candidates).
The Opportunity:
As a Senior Product Designer at Grafana Labs, you will join a growing Product Design organization of more than 25 designers, researchers, engineers, and design leaders distributed across six continents. You will work within a 100% remote R&D organization, so strong, proactive remote communication, collaboration, facilitation, and relationship building skills will be essential to your success.
As Senior Product Designer for Grafana Cloud’s Knowledge Graph, you'll design experiences for the context layer of Grafana Cloud that powers our entity graph, entity catalog and RCA workbench. Knowledge Graph automatically discovers services, infrastructure, and databases from the telemetry teams already have, maps how they depend on each other, and runs anomaly detection. This gives engineers, SREs, and their agents an up to date picture of their systems. We want anyone to be able to understand a system and resolve an incident faster, without writing queries or maintaining alert rules, not just the one person who happens to know it best.
Over time, you will develop deep expertise in your product area and associated customer and user personas, use cases, and workflows, which will enable you to design tailored, role-driven experiences.
You will also have an opportunity to contribute to the evolution of the Product Design team at Grafana by coaching and mentoring other designers, collaborating on team internal initiatives, and helping evolve new ways of working, learning, and having fun together as the team scales.
What You’ll Be Doing:
- Enabling customers to easily understand and explore how their systems connect to each other. Find clear, simple ways to show complex, constantly-changing information without overwhelming the user
- Translate research and data to experiences that are easy to digest and break down complexity
- Tailor the experience to different target audiences, covering multiple user perspectives
- Work cross-functionally with peers and leaders in engineering, product management, technical writing, and GTM functions, as well as other members of the Product Design team
- Prioritise for delivering impact while balancing business priorities, customer wishes and technical considerations
- Document user needs and pain points, design directions, UX trade-offs, and detailed designs for specific features and enhancements
- Execute research and contribute to quantitative and qualitative research initiatives with researchers, cross-functional collaborators, customers, and members of the Grafana user community
What Makes You a Great Fit:
- 7+ years of relevant design experience working on B2B/enterprise software products, ideally designing tools and services for developers or other highly technical users
- A portfolio of effective designs for complex products delivered in a fast-paced environment
- Experience running qualitative research in complex fields, building empathy with users and humans, their needs and pain points even when you have very little in common with them
- Ability to make design decisions that appropriately balance business goals, product priorities, customer feedback, research insights, and technical considerations
- Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams across multiple locations and time-zones to iteratively ship and evolve products while keeping the end design vision in mind
- Attention to detail and willingness to learn about a complex, very technical product space
- Experience working in a fully-remote, fast-paced environment where you are expected to share openly, default to transparency, and embrace your autonomy
Bonus Points For:
- Experience designing complex, data-dense interfaces with a focus on clarity
- Ability to rapidly gain an understanding of a technical domain and associated customer needs and user workflows in order to design effective experiences within that domain
- Domain knowledge or experience related to observability, cloud infrastructure, and/or database monitoring
- Experience helping design teams, especially at engineering led companies, level up their practice, collaboration with partner functions, and user and organizational impact
When you apply, please:
- Provide an example of an experience where decision-making in a complex area is made easy through a well-curated UI. Add a sentence or two about what you believe makes it effective.
Compensation & Rewards:
In Canada, the Base compensation range for this role is CAD $150,822 - CAD $180,986. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. All of our roles include Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), giving every team member ownership in Grafana Labs' success. We believe in shared outcomes—RSUs help us stay aligned and invested as we scale globally.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer, Security Assurance to join our GRC engineering team. - Experience securing large-scale distributed systems running in public clouds

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.
You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.
Staff Backend Engineer - Mimir Query, Databases
This is a remote position. We are looking for candidates in Canadian time zones.
What is Grafana Cloud?
Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, traces, and profiles with Grafana. It allows our customers to leverage the best open source observability software – including Prometheus, Mimir, Loki, Tempo, and Pyroscope – without the overhead of installing, maintaining and scaling their own observability stack.
The Databases team owns and operates the telemetry databases that are Mimir for metrics, Loki for logs, Tempo for traces, and Pyroscope for profiles. Our databases are offered as a hosted service in Grafana Cloud, and additionally as on-premise solutions with Grafana Enterprise Metrics, Grafana Enterprise Logs, and Grafana Enterprise Traces. They are multi-tenant distributed systems implemented in Go and operating at scale on Kubernetes across all major Cloud service providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a new perspective to the software.
Mimir Squad
The Mimir squad has 3 sub-squads, Ingest, Storage, and Query, which together maintain the Mimir OSS project, and additionally own and operate Grafana Cloud Metrics across 3 major cloud providers. Engineers on the team focus on optimizing the efficiency and resilience of processing, storing, and querying metrics at large volumes. These services operate at a large scale and performance is key to keeping the offering competitive and running smoothly.
A Mimir engineer has various work streams. They are likely engaged in a larger project with another engineer, and they are also incorporating some performance and reliability improvements discovered through operating the system in production. They are also responsible for writing and reviewing PRs and design documents from other engineers in the squad, shepherding automated release rollouts, and participating in the on-call rotation for their systems.
What will you be doing:
- Take an active role in influencing our roadmap and your own career objectives
- Work with your team to deliver new features, then use the results to iterate and improve.
- Drive projects from initial idea all the way to operations once it is in the hands of customers
- Embrace our open-source culture and contribute to other projects that may not directly fall within your team’s scope
- Design, build, operate, and maintain critical systems, owning the reliability, performance, and availability
- Be a part of your team’s follow-the-sun on-call rotations and take ownership of the services you’re running
- Support other team members, participate in design discussions and collaborate with the team
- Learn new skills by gaining a deeper understanding of our cloud product and our customers and getting to know the codebase of a large distributed system
We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction. We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always with strong code review and quality standards. You'll also have access to the latest frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.
What makes you a great fit:
You are a motivated self starter with a bias towards action. You are customer focused. We build everything with our users in mind. You have a passion for creating intuitive products that fit customers’ needs. You have good time management skills, which you leverage to work on the right things at the right time.
- Pragmatism: You are able to take on complex challenges and break them down to achieve short feedback loops: to analyze, design, and build modular solutions, deliver MVPs, gather data and feedback and then progress iteratively
- Collaboration and communication: The smallest unit we have is a squad. You’ll be working with your teammates in a fully remote setup. Good communication and time management skills are a must.
- Solid experience with at least one programming language. We use Go, but if you have familiarity with Python, C, C++, Rust or similar then that translates well
- Experience with leading and delivering projects from gathering requirements, brainstorming ideas all the way to shipping a product to the customer’s hands in a self-driven and collaborative way
- Experience with developing software that runs in the Cloud or experience with systems engineering
- Experience with being on-call and following the DevOps model
- Experience writing clean, robust, and performant software that is easily maintained by others
- Familiarity with observability systems, know when to use metrics, logs, traces, to debug a problem.
- Comfortable with microservices architecture and distributed systems
- Experience and comfort developing with LLMs like Claude and Codex on your day to day
Bonus Points For:
- Experience working with Kubernetes
- Experience working with queue systems, e.g. the Kafka protocol
- Been a user of Grafana and Prometheus in operational roles (including on-call for your team at a previous employer or just using these tools on hobby/homelab projects)
- Familiarity with the concept of infrastructure as code

Application Core Services (AppCore) is a group within Platform, in the Foundations department. We build and operate systems that support Grafana’s business operations and customer experience, working closely with product teams and internal business partners.

We are looking for a Staff Fullstack Engineer with strong backend experience who enjoys making complex business systems reliable, understandable and easier to operate. You will help deliver new capabilities while improving existing services, reducing repetitive manual work and addressing edge cases that affect customers and internal stakeholders.
This is a hands-on Staff engineering role within the AppCore Usage squad. You will lead complex technical work, contribute directly to implementation and share ownership with the squad’s other Staff and Senior engineers. Your primary focus will be Usage’s systems and outcomes, collaborating with adjacent teams when the work requires it.
Our ownership includes application code, data stores, deployment configuration and the cloud infrastructure supporting our services. You should be comfortable following a problem across those boundaries and making improvements with the appropriate platform teams.
We are remote-first and global. For this role, we prefer candidates in NASA’s Eastern Time zone to provide more overlap with our EMEA colleagues.
What You’ll Be Doing
Your initial focus will be approximately 75% backend and 25% frontend. This balance will evolve with the squad’s priorities. You should be comfortable delivering across the stack, from business logic and APIs through to the interfaces customers and internal teams use.
- Design, build and operate backend services and APIs supporting billing, rates, usage calculations, usage visibility and marketplace workflows.
- Build and maintain backend services primarily in Go, with Node.js also present in our stack, and contribute to TypeScript/React applications to deliver complete features.
- Improve the correctness and reliability of billing and usage workflows, including validation, reconciliation, error handling and recovery.
- Identify recurring manual tasks and replace them with maintainable automation, clear operational workflows and appropriate controls.
- Maintain and evolve the infrastructure supporting our services, including Kubernetes workloads, scheduled jobs, cloud resources and deployment configuration.
- Use infrastructure as code and automated delivery pipelines to make changes repeatable, reviewable and safe across environments.
- Investigate production issues across application code, databases and infrastructure, including resource exhaustion, failed jobs, slow queries and replication delays.
- Plan and execute service deployments, database changes and infrastructure migrations, including validation, monitoring and recovery plans.
- Build and maintain integrations with cloud marketplaces and external business systems where required by the squad’s work.
- Deliver projects from understanding requirements and proposing an approach through implementation, testing, rollout and production support.
- Make changes traceable and testable, supporting audit requirements and clear explanations of system behaviour.
- Collaborate with product management, Support, DealOps, GTM, infrastructure teams and adjacent AppCore squads to clarify requirements and resolve dependencies.
- Share technical leadership through design discussions, code reviews, mentoring and practical improvements.
- Participate in the squad’s on-call rotation after onboarding. Improve dashboards, alert quality, runbooks and recovery procedures, and follow through on incident findings.
What Makes You a Great Fit
You enjoy engineering work where correctness, reliability and business impact matter. You find value in improving an established system, removing a recurring operational problem or making a billing workflow easier to understand and support.
You take ownership from understanding the problem through delivery and production support. You can turn an ambiguous request into manageable increments, make sound trade-offs and follow through without needing each step prescribed. You ask useful questions, seek feedback and raise uncertainty or blockers early.
You adapt as priorities change, learn unfamiliar systems and technologies, and contribute where the squad needs you. You bring a strong backend specialty while remaining willing and able to work on frontend features and supporting infrastructure.
You reason about how a service behaves in production: how it is deployed, where its data lives, what happens when dependencies fail, and how the team detects and recovers from problems.
You communicate clearly in writing and in conversation. In a distributed team, you make decisions, progress and risks visible so colleagues can contribute across time zones. You work independently while staying connected to the squad.
As a Staff engineer, you bring technical depth and sound judgment while remaining close to implementation. You collaborate constructively with other experienced engineers, welcome different perspectives and help the squad reach decisions and move forward.
We embrace thoughtful use of AI-assisted development. We value engineers who use these tools to support exploration, implementation, testing and documentation while taking responsibility for the quality and correctness of the result.
Requirements
- Substantial experience designing, delivering and operating production backend systems, with the depth and judgment to lead complex work hands-on.
- Strong experience building and operating production backend systems in Go, our primary backend language.
- Professional experience contributing to frontend applications using TypeScript and React, or comparable technologies, and willingness to work across the stack as priorities change.
- Experience reasoning about distributed systems, including partial failures, retries, consistency and interactions between services.
- Experience with relational databases, including data modelling, schema migrations, query performance and safe production changes.
- Practical experience deploying and troubleshooting containerised services and jobs in Kubernetes.
- Experience managing cloud infrastructure through code and working with CI/CD pipelines, environment configuration and controlled rollouts.
- Ability to investigate production problems using logs, metrics and traces, and turn findings into lasting improvements.
- A record of delivering projects end to end, clarifying requirements, making trade-offs and following through after release.
- Experience working remotely, with clear asynchronous communication and dependable collaboration across time zones.
- Ability to learn unfamiliar domains and technologies, adjust your approach as new information emerges, and take ownership beyond your main area of expertise.
- Experience writing readable, well-tested software that other engineers can understand, maintain and operate.
- Willingness to participate in on-call and take responsibility for the production behaviour of the systems you build.
- Experience supporting colleagues through code reviews, mentoring and constructive technical discussions.
Bonus Points For
- Usage metering, billing engines, pricing and rates, financial reconciliation or customer-facing cost management applications.
- Reducing operational toil and automating workflows with recurring exceptions or manual interventions.
- Systems with auditability, traceability or financial-control requirements.
- MySQL operations, replication, database upgrades and performance tuning.
- Terraform, Jsonnet and Kubernetes deployment configuration.
- Argo Workflows or comparable deployment and job-orchestration tooling.
- Cloud infrastructure involving managed databases, object storage, service accounts and access controls, particularly on GCP.
- Data synchronisation pipelines and BigQuery integrations.
- Cloud marketplace integrations across AWS, Azure or GCP.
- Integrations with business platforms such as NetSuite or Salesforce.
- Observability tools such as Grafana, Prometheus, Loki or OpenTelemetry.

About the role:
Grafana Cloud runs Mimir, Loki, Tempo and Pyroscope as multi-tenant SaaS databases across AWS, GCP and Azure in regions worldwide. Our highest-SLA customers depend on them to run their businesses. We’re looking for a Staff Software Engineer to keep these systems reliable at scale.
The role combines building and operating. You’ll write the software, automation and product changes that make our databases more reliable, including changes to the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases where reliability calls for it. You’ll also be on call for our highest-SLA customers and handle the operational work that comes with it. You’ll bring a production mindset to product engineering and engineering rigor to reliability, and you’ll set technical direction across squads.
What You’ll Do
- Build reliability into the product. Write production code in our services, tooling and the Mimir, Loki and Tempo codebases that makes our databases more resilient, self-healing and scalable as demand grows quickly.
- Build automation and platform tooling that removes toil and scales our reliability practices across regions and cloud providers.
- Lead technical design. Author design docs, review others’ designs and PRs, and shape feature design so it’s scalable and operable from day one.
- Own the SLO framework. Define and evolve per-tenant SLOs and reliability models. Use SLO burn and incident learnings to find and fix the causes of failure in the systems themselves.
- Improve observability and alerting so we find problems before customers do, and so escalations are actionable rather than noisy.
- Be on call for our highest-SLA customers. Act as a technical escalation point for complex customer environments. Lead customer-impacting incident response, including customer bridge calls when needed, and write blameless post-incident reviews that lead to engineering fixes.
- Handle the operational work that comes from on-call. This includes investigating customer escalations, following up on incident actions, tuning capacity and configuration, and turning recurring issues into permanent fixes or automation.
- Multiply the team. Mentor engineers, teach reliability practices that teams adopt early in development, and work with engineering leadership on roadmaps and product strategy.
- We highly value those who are intellectually curious, who default to transparency, possess a high bias towards action, and who are also kind (this is important!)
On-Call

- 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant time building and owning distributed systems in production.
- Strong production software skills, ideally in at least one object-oriented language. You write clean, tested code and can make targeted changes in large open-source codebases you didn’t write.
- Deep understanding of distributed systems: performance, scaling and failure modes. You can reason about how a system will break before it does.
- Experience running multi-tenant systems at scale on Kubernetes in AWS, GCP or Azure, with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Helm or Jsonnet.
- Hands-on experience designing and implementing SLOs.
- Experience being on call for production systems. You troubleshoot calmly and methodically under pressure, and you’ve taken part in blameless incident response and written high-quality post-incident reviews.
- Staff-level technical leadership: driving cross-team projects, setting technical direction and making the engineers around you better.
- Working knowledge of Linux internals, networking and cloud storage.
Nice to Have:
-
- Experience with Mimir, Loki, Tempo, Pyroscope, Prometheus or other observability and time-series databases.
- Open-source contributions.
- Customer reliability engineering (CRE) or customer-facing escalation experience.

On-Call

Grafana Cloud is our composable observability platform that integrates metrics, logs, and traces with Grafana. The Observability department is focused on enabling developers to understand the health and performance of their applications and infrastructure in any environment by providing tools to instrument their code, ingest observability data into Grafana Cloud and visualize and explore it.
The OpenTelemetry SDKs team's mission is to make sure our users succeed in instrumenting their software with OpenTelemetry. We work closely with the OpenTelemetry SIGs to make OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation libraries a success. Members of this team are experts in at least one programming language and have a broad knowledge of various other programming languages.
In this role, you will focus on a language-specific implementation of OpenTelemetry in Python, with an emphasis on OpenTelemetry for Generative AI. You will get to work in an upstream-first approach, helping accelerate the OpenTelemetry project while bringing the innovations to Grafana labs products and offerings.
As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. You will bring your software engineering expertise to develop improvements to the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, with a strong focus on AI applications and agent workflows. This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI.
- Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions.
- Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality.
- Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability.
- Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community.

At Grafana Labs, Staff Engineers are defined by the impact they have and the people they enable. You take ownership of complex problems, set technical direction, and help others deliver improvements that matter to customers and the OpenTelemetry community.
- 8+ years of experience in software development, with strong proficiency in Python and experience debugging production software, language internals, libraries, and asynchronous code.
- An interest in AI applications and agent systems, and curiosity about how to instrument and troubleshoot them. Prior experience building AI systems is helpful, but not required.
- Experience working in open-source communities. You are eager to become an active member of the OpenTelemetry community, collaborate with maintainers and users, and keep learning across languages, frameworks, and the wider observability ecosystem.
- Familiarity with observability tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry, alongside experience with cloud-based software or systems engineering. You understand production environments and can assess operational risks.

The Observability department is focused on enabling developers to understand the health and performance of their applications and infrastructure in any environment by providing tools to instrument their code, ingest observability data into Grafana Cloud and visualize and explore it.
The OpenTelemetry SDKs team's mission is to make sure our users succeed in instrumenting their software with OpenTelemetry. We work closely with the OpenTelemetry SIGs to make OpenTelemetry SDKs and instrumentation libraries a success. Members of this team are experts in at least one programming language and have a broad knowledge of various other programming languages.
In this role, you will focus on a language-specific implementation of OpenTelemetry in Python, with an emphasis on OpenTelemetry for Generative AI. You will get to work in an upstream-first approach, helping accelerate the OpenTelemetry project while bringing the innovations to Grafana labs products and offerings.
As a company we are remote-first and global, we embrace people of different experiences and backgrounds to build diverse teams where every person brings a unique perspective to the software. We are looking for Engineers that are passionate about communicating with data and providing seamless experiences for our customers to join our growing team! Engineers at Grafana also have the opportunity to contribute to Open Source communities.
At Grafana Labs, ICs have a dedicated career path and do not have to become managers to progress in their career. Staff Software Engineers at Grafana have a large amount of experience across multiple areas. They are able to estimate, plan, coordinate and deliver large tasks spanning multiple systems. They actively coach and mentor other team members in their team and are able to identify and resolve issues with technology and product processes.
What You’ll Be Doing:
You will bring your software engineering expertise to develop improvements to the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, with a strong focus on AI applications and agent workflows. This is a hands-on role for someone with deep Python expertise and an interest in AI.
- Collaborate in open-source communities. You will develop and maintain the OpenTelemetry Python SDK and instrumentation libraries, working with maintainers and other vendors on specifications, APIs, and implementation decisions.
- Build Python instrumentation for AI agents. Build instrumentation that connects agent runs, model calls, and tool execution, including across asynchronous code. Contribute to evolving OpenTelemetry conventions for generative AI, with care for sensitive data and metric cardinality.
- Improve Python SDK performance. Use profiling and benchmarks to evaluate implementation approaches with the upstream community. Make sound tradeoffs around runtime overhead, compatibility, and maintainability.
- Be visible as an OpenTelemetry expert. Teach others, promote best practices around OpenTelemetry, semantic conventions, and various technologies and frameworks. Both within Grafana Labs and in the broader OpenTelemetry community.
- Support the technical direction and vision of the team, and contribute to business conversations on the OpenTelemetry strategy at Grafana Labs. Own projects from an ambiguous problem through design, implementation, testing, documentation, and release.
- Partner in an open and respectful way. Lend your knowledge and skills to our GTM, Product and Support teams. Join customer conversations, investigate instrumentation issues, and turn what you learn into fixes and practical guidance.
As we are remote-first and our engineering organization is largely remote, we provide guidance and meet regularly using video calls, so high agency and good communication skills are a must.
What Makes You a Great Fit:
At Grafana Labs, Staff Engineers are defined by the impact they have and the people they enable. You take ownership of complex problems, set technical direction, and help others deliver improvements that matter to customers and the OpenTelemetry community.
- 8+ years of experience in software development, with strong proficiency in Python and experience debugging production software, language internals, libraries, and asynchronous code.
- An interest in AI applications and agent systems, and curiosity about how to instrument and troubleshoot them. Prior experience building AI systems is helpful, but not required.
- Experience working in open-source communities. You are eager to become an active member of the OpenTelemetry community, collaborate with maintainers and users, and keep learning across languages, frameworks, and the wider observability ecosystem.
- Familiarity with observability tooling such as Grafana, Prometheus, and OpenTelemetry, alongside experience with cloud-based software or systems engineering. You understand production environments and can assess operational risks.
Bonus Points For:
- You have experience working on open source observability projects, ideally in OpenTelemetry or Prometheus.
- Experience in Python instrumentation techniques, profiling, runtime diagnostics, or asynchronous context propagation
- Experience in a hands-on technical leadership role, setting technical direction and leading project teams
- Experience instrumenting AI frameworks or agent workflows, or working with OpenTelemetry semantic conventions for generative AI
- Experience contributing to or maintaining Open Source projects, with evidence of successful pull requests and community collaboration
- Rust experience is a plus for exploring potential Python SDK performance improvements, including Rust-backed implementations.
Compensation & Rewards:
In the UK, the compensation range for this role is GBP 107,000 - GBP 134,000. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. jobs.description:
We are a global team of innovators and pioneers dedicated to shaping the future of observability. At New Relic, we build an intelligent platform that empowers companies to thrive in an AI-first world by giving them unparalleled insight into their complex systems. Your opportunity
As a Principal Product Designer on the UX Platform team, you will be the most senior individual design voice across the breadth of the UX Platform: the products our engineers and customers rely on every day, and the Design System that ties them together. You will partner closely with our Design Director as a trusted right hand, owning the hardest and most ambiguous problems, setting the quality bar, and helping decisions move so design is never the bottleneck.
Two things sit at the center of this role: designing for AI-native experiences, and rethinking how design itself gets done in AI-first workflows. We are fully immersed in both, and this role has a real hand in shaping where they go. We want someone genuinely eager to learn, test, and experiment here, but with the judgment to tell where AI raises the quality of the work and where it just adds noise. The aim is to use AI where it genuinely makes the work better, not to adopt it for its own sake.
You are a pragmatic optimist: ambitious about where we could go, honest about the terrain in front of us. You can hold “this is hard and might not work” and “let’s do it anyway, here’s how” in the same breath. You lead through craft and influence rather than authority, you take a vague problem and give it shape, you bring strong opinions but invite better ones, and you raise risks early and honestly. You lift the people around you by example, and the whole team’s work gets sharper because you are on it.
What you'll do
- Own the most complex and ambiguous design problems across our platform scope, from framing through detailed craft, end to end and with no oversight required.
- Design for AI-native experiences: shape interfaces that are non-deterministic and adapt to each use, design for outputs we cannot fully predict, and set the design principles and heuristics that keep those experiences coherent.
- Evolve how we design in AI-first, spec-driven workflows: help define how our role shifts, act as a multiplier for the team, and build ways to evaluate that we are shipping higher quality software, not just more of it.
- Set the bar for documentation and traceability: clear specs, references, and rationale that the team, our partners, and our AI tools can build on.
- Act as a second senior point of design judgment and a subject matter expert on our product: deputize for the Design Director in Product and Engineering reviews, shape strategic direction, and hold the quality bar across the whole product, not only your own area.
- Strengthen the connection between product design and the Design System, and define systems and processes that others across the company can benefit from.
- Partner with Product and Engineering to align on direction and keep work moving at a healthy cadence.
- Mentor designers, lead by example, and raise the overall level of craft across the team.
This role requires
- Extensive product design experience, including senior or lead work on complex software products.
- A portfolio that shows depth of craft and systems thinking across both product design and design systems, and recognized mastery of craft: a track record of raising the collective quality bar and defining patterns, systems, or processes that others adopt.
- A track record of owning ambiguous problems independently and driving them to real outcomes, end to end and without oversight.
- Comfort designing for AI-native, non-deterministic experiences, and enthusiasm for evolving how design gets done in AI-first workflows.
- A discerning approach to AI: eager to experiment, but with the judgment to tell where it adds real value, and a quality bar that does not bend for the sake of hype.
- Ability to act as a subject matter expert who shapes priorities, leads research where useful, and interprets analysis into design decisions.
- Proven ability to influence Product and Engineering partners without formal authority.
- Excellent written and verbal communication in English, and a habit of documenting decisions, rationale, and references clearly so that people and tools can build on them.
Bonus points if you have
- Experience designing services and platforms, especially in observability, developer tools, data, or complex B2B products.
- A technical background: an understanding of modern software architecture, and experience with data visualization.
- Experience contributing to or stewarding a design system at scale.
- Hands-on experience with spec-driven or AI-assisted design workflows.
- Comfort working in a distributed, cross-cultural team.

jobs.description:

Job Summary
Snyk's Product Security team works consultatively with the engineering teams that build and run our cloud platform: we identify the security requirements, agree together on what needs to change, and the owning teams implement it. As a Senior Product Security Engineer (Platform), you'll pair deep GCP and AWS infrastructure experience with AI coding agents to turn threat models into concrete Terraform, Kubernetes, and pipeline fixes, then work directly with platform teams to get those fixes merged. The goal is simple to state and hard to do well: make the secure option the easy option for the engineers building Snyk's platform.
About the Team
You'll join Snyk's Product Security team, which operates as an advisor rather than an owner: the cloud infrastructure teams retain ownership and operation of their systems, and Product Security's job is to find what needs to change and make that change easy to ship. The team sits close to Snyk's platform and infrastructure organization and is increasingly built around AI agents doing real infrastructure work, not just reviewing someone else's.
What You’ll Do
- Threat model Snyk's cloud infrastructure across GCP and AWS to identify the security requirements platform teams need to meet, then negotiate the resulting changes directly with the teams that own the systems.
- Use AI coding agents (for example Claude Code) to draft the Terraform, Kubernetes, and pipeline changes that fix identified security gaps, and raise them for the owning team to review and merge.
- Run agent-driven fixes at scale across many repositories, scoping every change so the owning platform team can review and merge it with confidence.
- Write and maintain the guidance AI agents rely on (skills, prompts, instruction files, security baselines) so agent output consistently matches Snyk's standards.
- Connect agents to live cloud, CSPM, and ticketing data through MCP servers, command-line tools, and provider APIs so their fixes are grounded in the real environment.
- Review AI-generated infrastructure changes critically: catch invented resources, unsafe defaults, and IAM permissions scoped wider than they need to be.
- Harden GCP identity and access management, including the resource hierarchy, IAM roles and conditions, service accounts and workload identity federation, and organization policy constraints, plus the AWS IAM equivalent.
- Improve Kubernetes and container security, primarily on GKE: cluster hardening (private clusters, Autopilot), RBAC, admission control, workload identity, network policy, and secure container image pipelines (Artifact Registry, Binary Authorization).
- Add automated security testing and CSPM tooling to CI/CD and GitOps pipelines, then help teams triage and fix what those tools surface.
- Benchmark infrastructure against secure configuration baselines such as the CIS Google Cloud Foundation Benchmark, and against the infrastructure controls in frameworks like ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53.
- Limit the risks AI agents themselves introduce: prompt injection, over-broad permissions, leaked secrets, and changes made without review.
- Measure whether agent-driven fixing is actually working across teams, and improve the approach as you learn what does and doesn't land.
What you’ll bring
- 5-8 years running or securing cloud infrastructure, ideally having built and operated production platforms on GCP or AWS before moving into security.
- Deep, hands-on GCP knowledge, including its security services, plus a good working knowledge of AWS; equivalent AWS IAM depth is a bonus.
- Strong grasp of GCP IAM: resource hierarchy (organization, folders, projects), IAM roles and conditions, service accounts and workload identity federation, organization policy constraints, and least privilege design.
- Practical Kubernetes and container experience, primarily GKE: cluster hardening (private clusters, Autopilot), RBAC, admission control, workload identity, network policy, and secure container images. EKS experience is also welcome.
- Comfort with infrastructure as code (for example Terraform) and automated deployment: CI/CD pipelines and GitOps.
- Solid DevSecOps practice: threat modeling, early shift-left testing, and continuous monitoring, plus the judgment to turn that into concrete infrastructure changes.
- Confidence using AI coding agents (for example Claude Code) day to day, including writing the guidance and prompts that keep their output reliable at scale.
- A critical eye for AI-generated infrastructure output: able to spot invented resources, unsafe defaults, and overly broad IAM permissions before anything ships.
- Comfort working consultatively: influencing and negotiating changes with teams who own and run the infrastructure, rather than owning it yourself.
- Nice to have: application security knowledge (for example code review, OWASP Top 10), or experience with Snyk's products or similar security testing tools.

Role Description
At Wiz, we're passionate about technical sales and helping our partners and their customers achieve maximum value. This starts with a team effort, collaborating with all available Wiz resources and teaming with the best partners in the world. Cloud transformation isn't slowing down, and with the explosion of autonomous AI agents, frontier models, and multi-tenant cloud architectures, the demand for next-generation MSP and MDR services is shifting overnight. We don't react to trends, we set the standard. As a Partner Solutions Architect (MSP), you won't just be supporting sales deals; you will influence and execute our technical MSP strategy from the ground up. Sitting at the absolute bleeding edge of technology, you will serve as the lead technical strategist empowering top-tier Managed Service Providers to rethink cloud security, package high-margin Wiz-powered offerings, and protect their clients' multi-cloud estates with the power of the Wiz Security Graph and our agentless architecture.
Responsibilities
- Drive technical strategy and solution development with MSP Partners
- Build and deliver world-class demos and technical enablement experiences for our partners.
- Architect an integrated solution and messaging, aligning with the MSP global team.
- Deeply engage with MSP Partner technical teams to build champions and identify opportunities to leverage technical integrations to drive deal acceleration.
- Serve as a technical evangelist and trusted advisor for cloud security, representing Wiz at partner and industry events.
- Assist partners in building a strong technical business delivery model around Wiz.
- Travel up to 40% of the time as needed.
Minimum qualifications
- 5+ Years of Cloud security expertise: Strong fluency in CSPM, CIEM, IaC security, containers, and serverless architectures.
- Deep hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, and/or Azure.
- DevSecOps & Supply Chain Security: Hands-on DevSecOps experience and deep familiarity with CI/CD processes, IaC tooling (Terraform, CloudFormation), and shifting security left.
- Systems & Identity Expertise: Solid foundation in operating systems, virtual machines, container orchestration, and cloud identity (IAM, access, certificates, keys).
- Sales Engineering Excellence: Proven track record in a technical pre-sales role delivering complex solutions and strategic storytelling to C-level executives at technology partners.
- Managed Services (MSP) DNA: Understanding of the MSP partner ecosystems. You know how MSPs build, price, and scale managed security offerings, manage SLAs, and drive technical adoption with internal engineering and SOC teams.
Preferred qualifications
- Managed AI Security & AI-SPM: Experience discovering shadow AI and securing cloud AI/ML workloads (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI, OpenAI, Anthropic) to help partners package and deliver managed AI security posture services to clients.
- Agentic Workflows & AI Guardrails: Familiarity with securing autonomous AI agents, agentic workflows, and emerging standards like Model Context Protocol (MCP) to define zero-trust access boundaries and runtime guardrails across client environments.
- SOC Efficiency & AI-Driven SecOps: Practical experience leveraging AI and automation to streamline multi-tenant SOC operations, accelerate incident triage, reduce alert fatigue, and automate remediation workflows.
- MDR & CNAPP Runtime Security: Experience with container security, eBPF, Kubernetes admission controllers, and real-time threat detection to power high-efficacy Managed Detection & Response (MDR) offerings.
- Managed DSPM & Regulatory Compliance: Experience implementing automated data discovery, lineage, and cloud data governance frameworks tailored to client compliance requirements (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, FedRAMP).

As one of the fastest-growing startups ever, we enable teams to secure cloud and AI applications by connecting code, cloud, and runtime into a single shared context. Trusted by security teams all over the world, we have a proven track record of success and a culture that values world-class talent. Not to mention, we're now powered by Google, meaning we offer our customers an AI-powered platform that harnesses Google’s Threat Intelligence and Security Operations to better detect, prevent, and respond to threats across all environments, allowing for further innovation.
Our Wizards from all over the globe work together to protect the infrastructure of our customers, including over 65% of the Fortune 100, who trust us to scan and secure over 230 billion files daily. We’re honored to be a leading player in a massive and growing market, and we continue to look for exceptional Wizards who are eager to make a significant impact on our team. At Wiz, you’ll have the freedom to think creatively, dream big, and use your full range of skills to contribute to our momentous growth. Come join our team and help us create secure cloud environments that allow even the best companies to move faster, all while having some fun!
Role Description
At Wiz, we're passionate about technical sales and helping our partners and their customers achieve maximum value. This starts with a team effort, collaborating with all available Wiz resources and teaming with the best partners in the world. Cloud transformation isn't slowing down, and with the explosion of autonomous AI agents, frontier models, and multi-tenant cloud architectures, the demand for next-generation MSP and MDR services is shifting overnight. We don't react to trends, we set the standard. As a Partner Solutions Architect (MSP), you won't just be supporting sales deals; you will influence and execute our technical MSP strategy from the ground up. Sitting at the absolute bleeding edge of technology, you will serve as the lead technical strategist empowering top-tier Managed Service Providers to rethink cloud security, package high-margin Wiz-powered offerings, and protect their clients' multi-cloud estates with the power of the Wiz Security Graph and our agentless architecture.
Responsibilities
- Drive technical strategy and solution development with MSP Partners
- Build and deliver world-class demos and technical enablement experiences for our partners.
- Architect an integrated solution and messaging, aligning with the MSP global team.
- Deeply engage with MSP Partner technical teams to build champions and identify opportunities to leverage technical integrations to drive deal acceleration.
- Serve as a technical evangelist and trusted advisor for cloud security, representing Wiz at partner and industry events.
- Assist partners in building a strong technical business delivery model around Wiz.
- Travel up to 40% of the time as needed.
Minimum qualifications
- 5+ Years of Cloud security expertise: Strong fluency in CSPM, CIEM, IaC security, containers, and serverless architectures.
- Deep hands-on experience with AWS, GCP, and/or Azure.
- DevSecOps & Supply Chain Security: Hands-on DevSecOps experience and deep familiarity with CI/CD processes, IaC tooling (Terraform, CloudFormation), and shifting security left.
- Systems & Identity Expertise: Solid foundation in operating systems, virtual machines, container orchestration, and cloud identity (IAM, access, certificates, keys).
- Sales Engineering Excellence: Proven track record in a technical pre-sales role delivering complex solutions and strategic storytelling to C-level executives at technology partners.
- Managed Services (MSP) DNA: Understanding of the MSP partner ecosystems. You know how MSPs build, price, and scale managed security offerings, manage SLAs, and drive technical adoption with internal engineering and SOC teams.
- Language skills: Proficiency in German, both written and spoken, is a bonus.
-
Preferred qualifications
- Managed AI Security & AI-SPM: Experience discovering shadow AI and securing cloud AI/ML workloads (AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex AI, OpenAI, Anthropic) to help partners package and deliver managed AI security posture services to clients.
- Agentic Workflows & AI Guardrails: Familiarity with securing autonomous AI agents, agentic workflows, and emerging standards like Model Context Protocol (MCP) to define zero-trust access boundaries and runtime guardrails across client environments.
- SOC Efficiency & AI-Driven SecOps: Practical experience leveraging AI and automation to streamline multi-tenant SOC operations, accelerate incident triage, reduce alert fatigue, and automate remediation workflows.
- MDR & CNAPP Runtime Security: Experience with container security, eBPF, Kubernetes admission controllers, and real-time threat detection to power high-efficacy Managed Detection & Response (MDR) offerings.
- Managed DSPM & Regulatory Compliance: Experience implementing automated data discovery, lineage, and cloud data governance frameworks tailored to client compliance requirements (HIPAA, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, FedRAMP).
Applicants must have the legal right to work in the country where the position is based, without the need for visa sponsorship. This role does not offer visa sponsorship.
Wiz is an equal opportunity employer. Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

We're looking for an experienced full-stack Documentation Platform Engineer to evolve our documentation site into a platform that delivers an exceptional experience for Tailscale's prospective and current customers.
You'll build, maintain, evolve, and support the platform and tools that internal teams and external contributors use to showcase Tailscale's features and products. This includes the documentation platform itself, our content pipelines, API documentation, and search. You'll work on a highly-visible customer-facing documentation site and you'll influence how documentation gets created, published, and consumed.

- Continuously improve and evolve our documentation site to create a helpful, delightful, and educational experience that helps homelabbers, developers, and enterprises (and their agents) get the most of out of Tailscale's products and features.

- Work cross-functionally with other engineering and product teams to integrate documentation with the Tailscale platform.
- Partner with designers, user research, and growth teams to implement designs and features as they move from experimentation to production.
- Help shape and tune a modern search and discovery infrastructure to help visitors, and agents, discover answers quickly.
- Work with open source contributors through GitHub discussions, issues, and pull requests.
- Monitor the platform's performance and maintain scalability for millions of visitors per month.
- Stay ahead of documentation trends through research, experimentation, and measuring results.

- You have a proven track record of building, extending, maintaining, and deploying documentation sites using static site generators like Hugo or Docusaurus, or documentation platforms built on NextJS, Astro, or other similar tools.

- You are fluent in TypeScript / JavaScript and React, and are comfortable with Python, command-line interfaces, shell scripting, and Git,
- You are comfortable with modern HTML and CSS and can implement designs provided by others.
- You have experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and automation for content or documentation workflows to reduce repetitive tasks and provide real-time feedback to authors.
- You can explain the impact and implications of LLMs as both tools for application development, and as consumers of content that documentation sites publish.
Nice to Have
- You have open source experience and are comfortable engaging with contributors on GitHub issues and pull requests.
- You understand how LLMs consume and interact with documentation.
- You understand multi-format content output (HTML, JSON, XML, raw Markdown, PDF, ePub

- Own the technical direction and architecture of Tailscale’s next-generation web console
- Build frontend infrastructure and platform capabilities that enable multiple Tailscale products to ship within a unified console experience
- Bring a special focus to identity-adjacent frontend systems, including authentication, session management, secure cross-origin integrations, and product surfaces that span multiple services
Because we’re a fully remote company building a highly technical product, we’re looking for someone who can move fluidly between product engineering and platform engineering. This role sits at an important intersection of user experience, browser security, developer tooling, and internal platform design. The ability to think strategically, make pragmatic architecture decisions, collaborate across engineering, design, growth, and infrastructure, and help other teams build with confidence is essential.

- Define and drive the frontend architecture for Tailscale’s next-generation console, including application structure, routing, state boundaries, shared abstractions, and long-term maintainability
- Design and maintain cross-origin authentication and session infrastructure between the console and other services, including auth flows, CORS policies, CSRF protections, cookie/session strategies, and support for multiple deployment environments
- Build and operate a frontend serving platform capable of hosting multiple Tailscale products under a unified development workflow
- Establish shared infrastructure, conventions, and design patterns that consolidate distinct product experiences into a cohesive console platform
- Create frontend architecture patterns, tooling, and abstractions that enable non-frontend engineers to build accessible, production-quality UI safely and efficiently
- Partner closely with Product Design to turn complex infrastructure and identity concepts into intuitive user experiences
- Collaborate with Growth, Design, Product, and other engineering teams on experimentation and iteration, including A/B testing, analytics instrumentation, and feature rollout strategies
- Define and improve frontend testing strategy across the console, including integration testing, end-to-end coverage, local developer ergonomics, and abstractions that reduce testing complexity for product teams
- Work with infrastructure and engineering tooling teams to improve local development workflows, build pipelines, preview deployments, release ergonomics, and operational reliability
- Raise the quality bar for frontend engineering across Tailscale through technical leadership, reviews, mentoring, and clear platform guardrails
- Required participation in our on-call rotation every x weeks, to triage and mitigate incidents
What We Are Looking For
- Deep experience building and operating production React applications at scale
- Strong understanding of web platform fundamentals, including HTTP semantics, browser security boundaries, authentication flows, cookies, storage, CORS, and CSRF
- Experience building internal platforms, frameworks, or shared libraries that enable other teams to ship products with strong guardrails
- Experience driving a unified console or platform vision across disparate frontend codebases
- Strong judgment around frontend architecture: knowing when to standardize, when to abstract, and how to keep systems understandable as they grow
- Experience designing scalable frontend testing strategies that improve confidence while hiding incidental complexity from product engineers
- Comfort collaborating across disciplines and functions, especially with design, growth, infrastructure, and developer tooling
- Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain tradeoffs and influence technical direction across teams
- A high degree of ownership and autonomy, with the ability to identify important problems and drive them through ambiguity

- Experience with design systems, component libraries, and connecting design tooling to production UI workflows
- Experience with feature flagging, analytics, experimentation systems, and progressive delivery patterns
- Experience working on identity, admin, B2B SaaS, or security-sensitive product surfaces

- Evolve and enhance the Tailscale connectivity offerings between clients, subnet routers, exit nodes and other integrations with customer network infrastructure.
- Provide architectural insights and resolve escalated customer network issues to fix complex connectivity problems.
- Collaborate with product management and internal engineering to develop integrated network solutions that prioritize scalability and ease of maintenance while ensuring a superior customer experience.
